points: Article 20 has three protections: no ex-post-facto criminal law (20(1)), no double jeopardy (20(2)), no self-incrimination (20(3)).
The protection in 20(2) applies only to proceedings before a court or judicial tribunal, not departmental proceedings (LX p133).

PYQ-POL-APK-F95A2E.lead: Option 3: the 2nd ARC's 10th Report (2008) is titled 'Refurbishing of Personnel Administration – Scaling New Heights'.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Improving the Personnel Administration
'Improving the Personnel Administration' is not the title of any 2nd ARC report; it is a made-up distractor.
Enhancing Personnel Administration: Some Insights
'Enhancing Personnel Administration: Some Insights' is not a 2nd ARC report title.
Refurbishing of Personnel Administration - Scaling New Heights
This is the exact title of the 10th Report of the Second ARC on personnel administration, submitted in November 2008.
The Future of Personnel Administration - Way Forward
'The Future of Personnel Administration – Way Forward' is not a 2nd ARC report title.

points: The 10th Report covered civil service recruitment, training, performance management and lateral entry.
The 2nd ARC gave 15 reports in all; the first was on Right to Information (2006).

PYQ-POL-B2BCE120AB04.lead: Option 2 (a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i) is correct: Article 137 lets the Supreme Court review its judgments, 226 gives High Courts writ power, 13 voids laws violating FRs, 32 is the right to move the Supreme Court.

head: List-I
Correct match (List-II)
Why / concept
rows: a. Article 137
ii. SC review of own judgments
Supreme Court may review its own judgments.
b. Article 226
iii. HC writs
High Courts issue writs for FRs and other legal rights.
c. Article 13
iv. Laws inconsistent with FRs void
Article 13 declares that laws inconsistent with, or taking away, Fundamental Rights are void to that extent; it is the textual base of judicial review over laws, so c matches iv.
d. Article 32
i. SC writs for FRs
Right to move the Supreme Court for FRs.

points: Option 1 fails: a-iii (HC writs) is wrong, a matches ii; b-iv (Laws inconsistent with FRs void) is wrong, b matches iii; c-ii (SC review of own judgments) is wrong, c matches iv.
Option 3 fails: b-i (SC writs for FRs) is wrong, b matches iii; d-ii (SC review of own judgments) is wrong, d matches i.

Option 4 fails: a-iv (Laws inconsistent with FRs void) is wrong, a matches ii; b-i (SC writs for FRs) is wrong, b matches iii; c-ii (SC review of own judgments) is wrong, c matches iv; d-iii (HC writs) is wrong, d matches i.
List-B text is missing from the stem; meanings are written from the Articles themselves.
PYQ-POL-B2BCE120AB04.also: Ambedkar called Art 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

PYQ-POL-B3D3C1FE136A.lead: Option 4: as of 2021 AFSPA was in force in many districts of Assam, Manipur and Nagaland — so 'All of the above'.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Assam
Assam: most of the State was a 'disturbed area' under AFSPA in 2021, so Assam alone is incomplete.
Manipur
Manipur: AFSPA covered the State except Imphal municipal area in 2021, so Manipur alone is incomplete.
Nagaland
Nagaland: the whole State was declared disturbed under AFSPA in 2021, so Nagaland alone is incomplete.
All of the above
All three States had AFSPA in many districts in 2021, so this is the complete answer.

points: AFSPA, 1958 gives the armed forces special powers in areas declared 'disturbed' by the Centre or the Governor.
From April 2022 the Centre reduced the disturbed areas in all three States.
PYQ-POL-B3D3C1FE136A.also: AFSPA was withdrawn from Tripura (2015) and Meghalaya (2018).

PYQ-POL-B4298A22F931.lead: Option 3: the Constitution now has 12 Schedules (it began with 8).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Wrong: 10 was the count after the 52nd Amendment (1985) added the Tenth Schedule, before the 11th and 12th came in 1992.
Wrong: the 73rd Amendment (1992) added the Eleventh Schedule, but the 74th Amendment added a Twelfth soon after.
Correct: four Schedules were added to the original 8 — Ninth (1st Amd, 1951), Tenth (52nd Amd, 1985), Eleventh (73rd Amd, 1992), Twelfth (74th Amd, 1992).
Wrong: no Thirteenth Schedule exists; the Constitution has 12 Schedules.

points: Memory hook: 8 + 1 (land reforms) + 1 (anti-defection) + 2 (Panchayats, Municipalities) = 12.
PYQ-POL-B4298A22F931.also: An earlier Tenth Schedule (Sikkim, 35th Amendment, 1974) was removed by the 36th Amendment (1975).

PYQ-POL-B629794CDF11.lead: Option 2: India is best described as unitary with federal features — federal in structure but with a strong unitary bias.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Truly Federal
Wrong: a truly federal system (like the USA) has equal, separate governments, dual citizenship and States that made the union; India has a strong Centre and single citizenship.
Unitary with Federal features
Correct: India has federal features (two levels of government, division of powers, independent judiciary) but many unitary features (strong Centre, emergency powers, Centre-appointed Governors).
Multi Federal
Wrong: 'multi federal' is not a recognised constitutional term.
Truly unitary
Wrong: a truly unitary system (like Britain) has only one government holding all power; India's States have their own constitutionally guaranteed powers.

points: K.C. Wheare called the Indian Union 'a unitary state with subsidiary federal features' (LX p204).
The Constitution itself never uses the word 'federation'; Article 1 calls India a 'Union of States'.
PYQ-POL-B629794CDF11.also: S.R. Bommai (1994): federalism is part of the basic structure.

PYQ-POL-B76F2C6AB4C3.lead: Option 4: the Seventh Schedule divides legislative power into three lists — Union, State and Concurrent.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Four lists
Wrong: residuary powers (Article 248) are not a fourth list; they are a separate power given to Parliament.
Two lists
Wrong: besides the Union and State Lists there is also a Concurrent List where both can make laws.
Five lists
Wrong: there is no five-list scheme in the Constitution.
Three lists
Correct: List I Union, List II State, List III Concurrent, distributed under Article 246.

points: Originally the lists had 97, 66 and 47 entries; the 42nd Amendment (1976) moved five subjects, including education and forests, from the State to the Concurrent List.
Vesting residuary powers in the Centre was borrowed from Canada (LX p68).

PYQ-POL-BB6B474E56B8.lead: Option 3: the First ARC was set up in January 1966.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1856 is before the 1857 revolt and long before independence; no ARC existed.
1947 is the year of independence; no ARC was set up then.
The First ARC was set up on 5 January 1966 under Morarji Desai (later K. Hanumanthayya).
1970 is when the First ARC finished its work (1966–1970), not when it was set up.

points: The First ARC recommended Lokpal and Lokayukta institutions (LX p709).
It also examined Centre-State relations and reported in 1969 (LX p223).
PYQ-POL-BB6B474E56B8.also: The Second ARC was set up in 2005 under Veerappa Moily.

PYQ-POL-BBC721689C5D.lead: Both statements are true, so the answer is option 3 (Both 1 and 2).

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: True
Britain follows parliamentary sovereignty, but India's Parliament is limited by a written Constitution, Fundamental Rights, the federal division of powers and judicial review.
True

Under Article 145(3), a case involving a substantial question of interpreting the Constitution is heard by a bench of at least five judges, called a Constitution Bench; British courts have no such power to strike down Acts.

points: Option 1 (1 only) fails because statement 2 is also true.
Option 2 (2 only) fails because statement 1 is also true.
Option 4 (neither) fails because both are true.
Even a constitutional amendment cannot destroy the basic structure (Kesavananda Bharati, 1973).

PYQ-POL-BF0035BF4852.lead: Option 1: the Constitution does not define which castes or tribes are SCs and STs; it leaves this to the President's lists.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: The Constitution does not define Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
True: Article 366 only says SCs/STs are those specified under Articles 341 and 342; it gives no criteria of its own.
Only religious minorities may establish educational institutions
False: Article 30 lets both religious and linguistic minorities set up and run educational institutions.
Minority institutions are exempt from State grants
False: Article 30(2) says the State shall not discriminate against minority institutions in giving aid; they are not excluded from grants.
Governors identify SCs and STs in their States
False: the President (after consulting the Governor) notifies SCs and STs for a State under Articles 341 and 342; Parliament alone can change the list.

points: Articles 341 and 342 are the key: President notifies, Parliament modifies by law.
Memory hook: 'Lists, not definitions'.

PYQ-POL-C2CEAD0B0FEC.lead: Option 2: tribal-majority regions notified by the President under the Fifth Schedule are called 'Scheduled Areas'.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Sub rural areas
'Sub rural areas' is a loose expression with no legal meaning in the Constitution.
Scheduled areas
'Scheduled Areas' are areas declared by the President under the Fifth Schedule (Article 244(1)) for special protection of tribals.
Gramalayas
'Gramalayas' is not a constitutional term; it is a distractor.
Suburban areas
'Suburban areas' means areas at the edge of cities; it has nothing to do with tribal protection.

points: The President can declare, increase, decrease or alter Scheduled Areas after consulting the Governor.
In the four North-East States (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram) the term used is 'Tribal Areas' under the Sixth Schedule.

PYQ-POL-C67A29A07228.lead: Option 3: Operation Sadbhavana is the Army's civic-action programme for people in remote areas.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Operation Sankalp
Operation Sankalp (2019) was the Indian Navy's deployment to protect Indian ships in the Gulf of Oman / Persian Gulf.
Operation Maitri
Operation Maitri (2015) was India's rescue and relief operation after the Nepal earthquake.
Operation Sadbhavana
Operation Sadbhavana is the Army's long-running goodwill programme in J&K, Ladakh and the North-East — schools, health camps, skill training and basic needs.
Operation Madad
Operation Madad (2018) was the Navy's flood rescue operation in Kerala.

points: Sadbhavana means 'goodwill': it aims to win hearts and minds by meeting local needs.
Memory hook: Sadbhavana = goodwill in remote areas.

PYQ-POL-C6F1BA933B69.lead: All five provisions have a bearing on education, so the answer is option 4 (1, 2, 3, 4 and 5).

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. DPSP
True
Article 45 (early childhood care and education) and Article 46 (education of SCs, STs, weaker sections) are Directive Principles on education.
2. Local bodies
True
The Eleventh Schedule (Panchayats) lists primary and secondary education, and the Twelfth Schedule (Municipalities) lists cultural and educational aspects.
3. Fifth Schedule
True
The Governor and Tribes Advisory Council look after the welfare and advancement of STs in Scheduled Areas, which includes their education.
4. Sixth Schedule
True
District Councils in tribal areas of the North-East can establish and manage primary schools (para 6).
5. Seventh Schedule
True
Education is Entry 25 of the Concurrent List after the 42nd Amendment (1976) shifted it from the State List.

points: Option 1 (1 and 2 only) and option 3 (1, 2 and 5 only) leave out the Fifth and Sixth Schedules, which also deal with education.
Option 2 (3, 4 and 5 only) leaves out DPSP and local bodies, which clearly mention education.
Article 21A (86th Amendment, 2002) also makes education for 6–14 years a Fundamental Right.

PYQ-POL-CCA760B85F25.lead: Option 2: the Third Schedule contains the forms of oaths and affirmations.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: First Schedule
The First Schedule lists the States and Union Territories with their territories.
Third Schedule
The Third Schedule gives forms of oaths/affirmations for Union and State ministers, MPs, MLAs, judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, and the CAG.
Second Schedule
The Second Schedule deals with salaries, allowances and privileges of the President, Governors, Speakers, judges, CAG etc.
Fourth Schedule
The Fourth Schedule allocates Rajya Sabha seats to States and UTs.

points: The oaths of the President (Article 60), Vice-President (Article 69) and Governor (Article 159) are written in the Articles themselves, not the Third Schedule.
Memory hook: Third = Oath (you swear 'three times').

PYQ-POL-CE682255AA3F.lead: Option 2: K.C. Wheare described India as 'quasi-federal'.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: A cooperative federation
'Cooperative federation' is Granville Austin's description of Indian federalism, not Wheare's.
A quasi-federation
K.C. Wheare called India quasi-federal — 'a unitary state with subsidiary federal features rather than a federal state with subsidiary unitary features' (LX p204).
A strong union
'A strong union' is not Wheare's phrase; Ivor Jennings spoke of 'a federation with a strong centralising tendency'.
Not a federation
Wheare did not deny that India is a federation; he called it 'quasi' (partly) federal.

points: 'Quasi' means 'almost' or 'partly' — federal in form but with strong unitary features.
PYQ-POL-CE682255AA3F.also: Others: Paul Appleby — 'extremely federal'; Morris Jones — 'bargaining federalism' (LX p204).

PYQ-POL-CF64733B838A.lead: Option 3: Cri-MAC (Crime Multi-Agency Centre) shares real-time information on heinous crimes, including human trafficking.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: ITSSO
ITSSO (Investigation Tracking System for Sexual Offences) monitors time-bound investigation of sexual offence cases.
NDSO
NDSO (National Database on Sexual Offenders) is a database of persons convicted of sexual offences.
Cri-MAC
Cri-MAC, launched by MHA in March 2020, gives real-time alerts on heinous crimes and inter-state criminals among police forces over the CCTNS network.
SPUWAC
SPUWAC (Special Police Unit for Women and Children) is a Delhi Police unit, not an MHA real-time crime platform.

points: Key word in the stem: 'real-time information' — only Cri-MAC is a live alert-sharing system.
NDSO and ITSSO are both about sexual offences, not trafficking alerts.

PYQ-POL-CFAE00F9470C.lead: Option 1: the Fifth Schedule deals with Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in all States other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Fifth Schedule
The Fifth Schedule (Article 244(1)) covers the administration and control of Scheduled Areas outside the four North-East States.
Sixth Schedule
The Sixth Schedule (Article 244(2)) covers tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram through Autonomous District Councils.
Ninth Schedule
The Ninth Schedule protects listed laws from judicial review (Article 31B).
Seventh Schedule
The Seventh Schedule contains the Union, State and Concurrent Lists.

points: Andhra Pradesh's tribal areas (e.g. ASR district) are Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule.
Memory hook: Sixth Schedule = the four North-East States A-M-T-M (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram); Fifth Schedule = rest of India.

PYQ-POL-D4B49C302327.lead: Option 2: Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Australian
Australia gave the Concurrent List and the joint sitting of both Houses, not DPSP.
Irish
Ireland gave DPSP, nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha and the method of electing the President.
German
Germany (Weimar) gave the suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency.
Austrian
Austria is not a listed source of any major feature of the Indian Constitution.

points: Ireland had itself copied the idea from the Spanish Constitution.
DPSP are non-justiciable (Article 37) but fundamental in governance.

PYQ-POL-DD1DF0F1519E.lead: Option 1: an independent judiciary is essential to a federation because it settles disputes between the Centre and the States.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Independence of judiciary from executive and legislature
Correct: in a federation powers are divided by a written Constitution, so an independent umpire (the Supreme Court, Article 131) is needed to settle Centre-State disputes.
Elected representatives of the people in the Union Legislature
Wrong: elected representatives exist in unitary countries too (e.g. the UK), so this is a feature of democracy, not federalism.
Union Cabinet can have a minister from a regional political party
Wrong: a minister from a regional party is a coalition politics practice, not a structural feature of federalism.
Fundamental rights of the citizens enforceable by courts
Wrong: court-enforceable Fundamental Rights are a feature of constitutional democracy; unitary states can also have them.

points: Essential federal features: dual polity, division of powers, written and rigid Constitution, supremacy of the Constitution, independent judiciary, bicameralism.

PYQ-POL-DD2A242ED111.lead: Option 3: GeM (Government e-Marketplace) is the one-stop online portal for buying goods and services by government bodies and PSUs.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: e-Procure
'e-Procure' is a generic name for e-tender portals (like the Central Public Procurement Portal), not the one-stop marketplace.
e-Biz
e-Biz was a government portal for business licences and approvals, not procurement.
GeM
GeM was launched in August 2016 by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and replaced DGS&D for common-use goods and services.
GeP
'GeP' is not the name of any government procurement platform; it is a distractor.

points: GeM brings transparency and speed to public buying through online bidding and reverse auctions.

PYQ-POL-DF9FF2456DD0.lead: Option 1: AP Act 2 of 1998 set up the Andhra Pradesh State Road Development Corporation (APRDC).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: A.P. State Road Development Corporation
APRDC was created by AP Act 2 of 1998 to develop, maintain and raise funds for the State's core road network.
A.P. State Road Transport Corporation
APSRTC was set up in 1958 under the central Road Transport Corporations Act, 1950, not a 1998 State Act.
A.P. Road Sector Project
The AP Road Sector Project is a World Bank-assisted programme, not a body created by an Act.
A.P. Highway Development Project
'AP Highway Development Project' is a programme name, not a statutory body created by this Act.

points: A statutory corporation is created by a law passed by the legislature; programmes and projects are executive schemes.

PYQ-POL-DFFD1CA4C18D.lead: Option 2: tribal-majority areas notified under the Fifth Schedule are called 'Scheduled Areas'.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Metropolitan areas
Wrong: metropolitan areas are big cities; Scheduled Tribes are not identified with them.
Scheduled areas
Correct: Scheduled Areas are declared by the President under the Fifth Schedule (Article 244(1)) to protect tribal land, culture and self-rule.
Forest areas only
Wrong: many tribals live in forests, but 'only' is too absolute and 'forest area' is not the constitutional term.
Rural areas only
Wrong: tribals live in rural and urban areas; 'only' is too absolute and this is not the constitutional term.

points: PESA Act, 1996 extends Panchayati Raj to Fifth Schedule areas with special powers to the Gram Sabha.
Watch for absolute words like 'only' — they usually make an option wrong.

PYQ-POL-E70408F29CF7.lead: Option 4: Indian federation is NOT the result of an agreement among the States.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: There is an independent judiciary in India
Is a feature: the Supreme Court is independent and settles Centre-State disputes (Article 131).
Powers have been clearly divided between the Centre and the States
Is a feature: the Seventh Schedule divides powers into Union, State and Concurrent Lists.
The federating units have been given unequal representation in the Rajya Sabha
Is a feature: under the Fourth Schedule Rajya Sabha seats are given by population, so States have unequal representation (unlike the equal US Senate).
It is the result of an agreement among the federating units
Not a feature: unlike the USA, India did not come from an agreement among States; States have no right to secede, and Ambedkar called it a 'Union' because it is indestructible.

points: Parliament can change the boundaries or names of States by law (Article 3).
The question has NOT: the ✓ marks the false claim about Indian federalism.

PYQ-POL-E8D8F527A635.lead: Option 2: Dr B.R. Ambedkar said the Constitution 'could be both unitary as well as federal according to the requirements of time and circumstances'.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Nehru
Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution; this quote about flexible federalism is not his.
Ambedkar
Ambedkar said this in the Constituent Assembly while explaining that the Constitution avoids the 'tight mould of federalism' (LX p204).
Appleby
Paul Appleby described the Indian system as 'extremely federal', not this quote.
Patel
Sardar Patel led the integration of princely States; this quote is not his.

points: Example: in an emergency, Parliament can make laws on State List subjects (Article 250), so the system becomes unitary.

PYQ-POL-E92A1C55334B.lead: Option 3: Cri-MAC (Crime Multi-Agency Centre) gives real-time information on heinous crimes, including human trafficking.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: ITSSO
ITSSO tracks time-bound investigation of sexual offence cases; it is not a real-time crime alert system.
NDSO
NDSO is a national database of convicted sexual offenders, not a live alert system.
Cri-MAC
Cri-MAC, launched by MHA in 2020 over CCTNS, shares real-time alerts on heinous crimes and inter-state criminals among police forces.
SPUWAC
SPUWAC is a Delhi Police special unit for women and children, not an MHA IT initiative.

points: Key word: 'real-time' — only Cri-MAC is a live alert-sharing network.

PYQ-POL-EBC124C51BB7.lead: Option 1: both statements are true, and Statement-II explains Statement-I.

head: Part
True/False
Why
rows: Statement-I
True
'Prisons' is Entry 4 of the State List (Seventh Schedule), so each State runs its prisons with its own jail manuals and rules.
Statement-II
True
The Prisons Act, 1894 is still the basic law, and it placed prisons under the control of the Provincial (now State) Governments.

points: Does II explain I? Yes — States manage prisons today because the 1894 Act (and later the Constitution) left the subject with the provinces/States.
Option 2 fails because II does explain I; options 3 and 4 fail because both statements are true.
PYQ-POL-EBC124C51BB7.also: MHA prepared a Model Prisons and Correctional Services Act, 2023 to guide States.

PYQ-POL-F0DA2390EAEB.lead: Option 2: the British interfered in princely States' internal administration to give effect to their international commitments.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Never interfered
Wrong: under paramountcy the British did interfere, so 'never' is false.
V For giving effect to its international commitments
Correct: since the Crown controlled the States' foreign relations, it interfered internally when needed to honour India's international commitments (and also for gross misrule).
On the request of the Congress party
Wrong: the Congress had no legal standing with the princely States, so its request was never a ground.
On the request of the people
Wrong: the people of the States had no legal right to invite British interference.

points: Paramountcy lapsed under the Indian Independence Act, 1947, and States then joined India by Instruments of Accession.

PYQ-POL-F19628A9108E.lead: Option 2: Scheduled Castes are popularly called 'Dalits' today.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Harijans
'Harijan' ('people of God') was Gandhi's term; governments now advise against using it, so it is not the current popular name.
Dalits
'Dalit' means 'oppressed' and is the widely used present-day name for Scheduled Castes.
Adivasis
'Adivasi' means 'original dwellers' and refers to tribal people (Scheduled Tribes), not SCs.
Backwards
'Backwards' usually refers to Other Backward Classes (OBCs), not SCs.

points: The constitutional term is 'Scheduled Castes' under Article 341; 'Dalit' is a popular, not legal, term.

PYQ-POL-F2062E0E2FE6.lead: Option 1: universal adult franchise gives every adult citizen the right to vote, subject to limits laid down by law.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: To provide a right to vote to all citizens of India, subject to limitations conferred by statute
Correct: Article 326 says Lok Sabha and Assembly elections are on adult suffrage; a law can disqualify on grounds like unsound mind, crime or corrupt practice.
To cater to the needs of senior citizens of India
Wrong: the vote is for all adults (18+), not a scheme for senior citizens.
To guarantee employment for at least one person in a family
Wrong: guaranteed employment is a welfare scheme (like MGNREGA), not adult franchise.
To provide uniform health care system in India
Wrong: health care has nothing to do with the right to vote.

points: The 61st Amendment (1988) reduced the voting age from 21 to 18.
'Universal' means no exclusion by caste, religion, sex, property or education.

PYQ-POL-F63E2D6F5147.lead: Option 1: the Government of India Act, 1935 had the most profound influence on the Constitution.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: The government of India act, 1935
Correct: about 250 provisions came from the 1935 Act — federal scheme, Governor's office, judiciary, Public Service Commissions, emergency provisions and administrative details (LX p69).
The U. S. constitution
Wrong: the US Constitution gave Fundamental Rights and judicial review, but far fewer provisions.
The British constitution
Wrong: the British Constitution gave the parliamentary system and rule of law, which shaped the political part but not most of the text.
The U. N. Charter
Wrong: the UN Charter influenced Article 51 (international peace) at most; it was not a major source.

points: The structural part of the Constitution is largely from the 1935 Act; the philosophical part from the US and Irish Constitutions (LX p49).
Article 395 repealed the 1935 Act and the Indian Independence Act, 1947.

PYQ-POL-F7DE0861C334.lead: Official key: option 2 (A, B and D). But the 2nd ARC reports support only A and B, i.e. option 3.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: A
True
The 4th Report 'Ethics in Governance' (2007) recommended that corrupt public servants be made liable to pay damages for loss caused to the State.
B
True
The 4th Report recommended a law to protect whistle-blowers who expose corruption.
C
False
The 2nd ARC recommended abolishing discretionary funds of legislators (MPLADS/MLALADS), not continuing them.
D
False
The 1st Report on Right to Information (2006) recommended repealing the Official Secrets Act, 1923, not restoring it.

points: Option 1 (A and C) fails because C is false.
Option 2 (A, B and D), the official key, includes D, which goes against the ARC's actual recommendation.
Option 4 (C and D) fails because both C and D are false.
Option 3 (A and B only) matches the ARC reports.
PYQ-POL-F7DE0861C334.also: Disputed key: the 2nd ARC recommended repealing, not restoring, the Official Secrets Act, so D is wrong and the correct set is A and B only (option 3).

PYQ-POL-FF781653DBBA.lead: Option 4: Scheduled Castes are commonly called 'Dalits'.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Indigenous classes
'Indigenous classes' is not a term used for SCs; 'indigenous' usually describes tribal peoples.
Adivasis
'Adivasis' means 'original dwellers' and refers to Scheduled Tribes, not SCs.
Minorities
'Minorities' are religious or linguistic groups protected under Articles 29–30, a different category.
Dalits
'Dalit' ('oppressed') is the popular present-day name for Scheduled Castes.

points: The legal term remains 'Scheduled Castes', notified by the President under Article 341.

PYQ-POL-WEB-03617C.lead: Option 2 (2, 3, 4, 1): Sri Lanka (1931), Japan (1945), India (1950), USA (1965).

head: Country
Year
Why
rows: Sri Lanka
The Donoughmore Constitution of 1931 gave universal adult franchise to Ceylon, the first in Asia.
Japan
Japan's 1945 election-law reform gave all adults, including women, the vote (first used in 1946).
India
The Constitution (Article 326) gave universal adult franchise from 26 January 1950.
USA
US women got the vote in 1920 (LX p69), but racial barriers to voting were removed only by the Voting Rights Act, 1965.

points: Option 1 (1,2,3,4) and option 3 (1,3,4,2) wrongly put the USA first.
Option 4 (3,4,1,2) puts Sri Lanka last, though it was earliest.

PYQ-POL-WEB-187E6D.lead: Option 4: State of Kerala v. Leesamma Joseph (2021) deals with reservation in promotion for persons with disabilities.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Dowry
Wrong: the case is not about dowry; it concerns persons with disabilities.
The economic weaker section
Wrong: the case is not about the EWS quota (103rd Amendment, 2019).
Education
Wrong: the case is not about education rights.
Persons with disabilities
Correct: the Supreme Court held that persons with disabilities are entitled to reservation in promotion, even if they were recruited without it.

points: The ruling relied on the Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995 (now the RPwD Act, 2016).

PYQ-POL-WEB-2620F8.lead: Option 1: the Constitution establishes an independent (and single integrated) judicial system.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Independent judicial system
Correct: the Constitution keeps judges free from executive and legislative control through security of tenure, fixed service conditions and separation of judiciary from executive (Article 50).
Plural judicial system
Wrong: 'plural judicial system' (many parallel court systems) does not describe India.
Dual judicial system
Wrong: a dual judicial system (separate federal and state courts) exists in the USA; India has one integrated system with the Supreme Court at the top.
Partial judicial system
Wrong: 'partial judicial system' is not a constitutional term.

points: Integrated: Supreme Court → High Courts → subordinate courts enforce both Central and State laws.

PYQ-POL-WEB-2F4165.lead: Option 1: the Union List covers matters of national importance like defence and foreign affairs.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Union
Correct: List I (Union List) has subjects like defence, foreign affairs, banking, currency and atomic energy; only Parliament can legislate on them.
State
Wrong: List II (State List) has local subjects like police, public order, public health and agriculture.
Concurrent
Wrong: List III (Concurrent List) has shared subjects like education, forests and marriage.
Residuary
Wrong: residuary is not a list; Article 248 gives Parliament power over subjects not in any list.

points: Memory hook: Union = whole Nation matters.

PYQ-POL-WEB-2F580E.lead: Option 1: the First Amendment Act, 1951 added the Ninth Schedule.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: First Amendment
Correct: the First Amendment (1951) added the Ninth Schedule along with Articles 31A and 31B to protect land reform laws from challenge.
Eighth Amendment
Wrong: the Eighth Amendment (1960) extended SC/ST and Anglo-Indian reservation in legislatures.
Ninth Amendment
Wrong: the Ninth Amendment (1960) transferred Berubari to Pakistan under the Nehru-Noon agreement.
Forty second Amendment
Wrong: the 42nd Amendment (1976) made big changes (e.g. 'socialist, secular') but added no Schedule.

points: I.R. Coelho (2007): laws added to the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 can be reviewed for violating the basic structure.

PYQ-POL-WEB-2F860A.lead: Option 1: Article 39(b) directs that ownership and control of the material resources of the community be distributed to best serve the common good.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?

Correct: Article 39(b) is about distributing material resources of the community for the common good.
Article 39(a)
Wrong: Article 39(a) is about the right to an adequate means of livelihood for all citizens.
Article 39(c)
Wrong: Article 39(c) is about preventing concentration of wealth and means of production.
Article 39(d)
Wrong: Article 39(d) is about equal pay for equal work for men and women.

points: 39(b) and 39(c) together were protected by Article 31C (25th Amendment, 1971).
PYQ-POL-WEB-2F860A.also: Property Owners Association (2024): not every private resource is a 'material resource of the community'.

PYQ-POL-WEB-375135.lead: Only statement 2 is correct, so the answer is option 2 (2 only).

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. No provision for equal pay for men and women
False
Article 39(d), a Directive Principle, directs the State to secure equal pay for equal work for both men and women, so a provision does exist.
2. Constitution does not define 'backward classes'
True
Articles 15(4), 16(4) and 340 use the term but never define it; identifying backward classes is left to the State and to commissions like Kalelkar and Mandal.

points: Option 1 fails because statement 1 is false (Article 39(d) exists).
Option 3 fails because it includes the false statement 1; option 4 fails because statement 2 is true.
Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 gave effect to Article 39(d); it is now merged into the Code on Wages, 2019.

PYQ-POL-WEB-39A25F.lead: The original Constitution had 395 Articles (option 1), in 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.

Correct?

Not the original count; another distractor near 395.

points: Even today the last Article is still numbered 395, because new Articles are inserted with letters (e.g. 21A, 243A) instead of renumbering.

Memory hook: 395 – 22 – 8 (Articles – Parts – Schedules) in 1949.
PYQ-POL-WEB-39A25F.also: The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.

PYQ-POL-WEB-44365F.lead: Bhojpuri (option 4) is NOT in the Eighth Schedule.

What it is / means
Correct?

✗ (included)

✗ (included)
Bhojpuri
Not in the Eighth Schedule; its inclusion is still only a demand.

points: The Eighth Schedule now lists 22 languages; the original Constitution had 14.

Memory hook: Bhojpuri and Rajasthani are frequent 'not included' answers.
PYQ-POL-WEB-44365F.also: 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; 92nd (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali.

PYQ-POL-WEB-51D9B4.lead: The Fourth Schedule allocates seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) — option 4.

This is the Eighth Schedule (22 languages).

The Fourth Schedule allocates Rajya Sabha seats to States and Union Territories (Articles 4 and 80).

points: Rajya Sabha seats are given to States mainly on the basis of population, so big States get more seats.

PYQ-POL-WEB-57B35F.lead: Article 350-A (option 3) deals with mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage.

What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Article 349
Special procedure for enacting certain laws relating to language.

Every State shall endeavour to provide instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to linguistic minority children.
Article 351
Directive for the development of the Hindi language.

points: Articles 350-A and 350-B were added by the 7th Amendment, 1956.

PYQ-POL-WEB-57B35F.also: Article 350-B provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

PYQ-POL-WEB-6F66BE.lead: Article 1 (option 2) declares India a 'Union of States'.

What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Article 14
Equality before law and equal protection of laws.
Article 1
India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.
Article 3
Parliament can form new States and alter boundaries or names.
Article 5
Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.

points: Dr. Ambedkar explained 'Union' shows the federation is not the result of an agreement among States, and no State can secede.
Article 1 also names the country 'India, that is Bharat'.

PYQ-POL-WEB-799537.lead: Banking (option 1) is in the Union List, so it is a Central subject.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Banking
Union List subject (Seventh Schedule) — only Parliament makes laws on it.
Agriculture
State List subject, so mainly the States make laws on it, not the Centre.
Prisons
State List subject (prisons and reformatories), so it comes under the States, not the Centre.
Public Health
State List subject (public health and sanitation).

points: The Seventh Schedule under Article 246 has three lists: Union, State and Concurrent.
Subjects of national importance needing uniform rules (banking, defence, currency) go to the Union List.

PYQ-POL-WEB-79DD67.lead: The people (option 4) are the chief source of political power in India.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: The Constitution
It is the supreme law, but it was itself given by the people ('We, the people... give to ourselves this Constitution').
The Parliament
Parliament only exercises power granted by the Constitution.
Parliament and State Legislature
Both exercise delegated power under the Constitution; they are not the source.
The People
The Preamble shows the people of India are the ultimate source of authority.

points: The Preamble begins 'We, the people of India' — authority flows from the people.
People exercise this power through elections by adult suffrage (Article 326).
The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949.

PYQ-POL-WEB-8017C7.lead: Independence of judiciary came from the USA (option 4).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: France
Gave the Republic and ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity.
Britain
Gave parliamentary government and the Rule of Law.
Ireland
Ireland gave the Directive Principles, not independence of judiciary.
The USA
Gave independence of judiciary, judicial review and Fundamental Rights.

points: Removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges is also modelled on the US.
Independence is protected by security of tenure, fixed salaries charged on the Consolidated Fund and the ban on practice after retirement.

PYQ-POL-WEB-858199.lead: Article 263 (option 4) provides for inter-State coordination through an Inter-State Council.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Article 32
Right to constitutional remedies — writs by the Supreme Court.
Article 360
Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency, not co-operation between States.
Article 14
Article 14 gives equality before law and equal protection of laws; it is not about inter-State co-operation.
Article 263
President may set up an Inter-State Council to coordinate between States and the Centre.

points: The Council inquires into disputes, discusses common subjects and recommends better policy coordination.
It was first set up in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation.

PYQ-POL-WEB-89B39C.lead: Option 2 is NOT correctly matched: oaths and affirmations are in the Third Schedule, not the Second.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?

Correct pair: the Eighth Schedule lists the languages recognised by the Constitution, now 22.
matched
Second – Oaths and affirmations
Wrong pair: Second covers emoluments of President, Governors, judges, CAG; oaths are Third
✓ (answer)

matched
Tenth – Anti-defection
Correct pair: added by 52nd Amendment, 1985
matched

points: In a "not correctly matched" question, the answer is the one wrong pair.

PYQ-POL-WEB-968646.lead: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission was set up in 1953 (option 2).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Year of Independence; no backward classes commission then.
The First Backward Classes Commission under Kaka Kalelkar was appointed in January 1953 under Article 340.
Year of the States Reorganisation Act; the Kalelkar report had already been given in 1955.
No backward classes commission was set up that year.

points: It was appointed by the President under Article 340 and reported in 1955.
The Second Backward Classes Commission was the Mandal Commission (1979).
PYQ-POL-WEB-968646.also: The Second Backward Classes Commission was the Mandal Commission (1979).

PYQ-POL-WEB-9A4983.lead: Maharashtra (option 2) first established the Lokayukta, in 1971.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Odisha
Passed a Lokayukta Act in 1970, but the institution actually started only in 1983.

First State to establish the Lokayukta, in 1971.
Bihar
Set up its Lokayukta only after Maharashtra (1971).
Andhra Pradesh
Set up its Lokayukta only after Maharashtra (1971).

points: Trap: Odisha passed the law first (1970), but Maharashtra first set up the office (1971).

PYQ-POL-WEB-9A4983.also: The central Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act was passed in 2013.

PYQ-POL-WEB-A13881.lead: Option 1 (a-IV b-III c-I d-II) is correct: a reprieve stays execution, a respite gives a lesser sentence for a special reason, a remission cuts the period, and a commutation changes the type of punishment.

head: List-I
Correct match (List-II)
Why / concept
rows: a. Reprieve
IV. Stay of execution
Temporary stay of execution (e.g. death sentence) pending pardon.
b. Respite
III. Lesser sentence for special reasons
Lesser sentence due to special fact like pregnancy.
c. Remission
I. Reduce amount, same character
Remission reduces the period (amount) of a sentence without changing its character, for example two years' rigorous imprisonment cut to one year, so c matches I.
d. Commutation
II. Substitute lighter form
Change type, e.g. death to life imprisonment.

points: Option 2 fails: a-I (Reduce amount, same character) is wrong, a matches IV; b-II (Substitute lighter form) is wrong, b matches III; c-III (Lesser sentence for special reasons) is wrong, c matches I; d-IV (Stay of execution) is wrong, d matches II.
Option 3 fails: b-II (Substitute lighter form) is wrong, b matches III; c-III (Lesser sentence for special reasons) is wrong, c matches I; d-I (Reduce amount, same character) is wrong, d matches II.

Option 4 fails: a-III (Lesser sentence for special reasons) is wrong, a matches IV; b-I (Reduce amount, same character) is wrong, b matches III; c-II (Substitute lighter form) is wrong, c matches I; d-IV (Stay of execution) is wrong, d matches II.
PYQ-POL-WEB-A13881.also: President's pardoning power is Article 72; Governor's is Article 161.

PYQ-POL-WEB-AB79B2.lead: Compelling a person to incriminate himself is self-incrimination (option 3).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Double jeopardy
Being prosecuted and punished twice for the same offence — barred by Article 20(2).
Ex post facto law
A law that punishes an act retrospectively — barred by Article 20(1).
Self-incrimination
Forcing an accused person to be a witness against himself — barred by Article 20(3).
Estoppel
A rule of evidence: a person cannot deny a stand he earlier took and others relied on.

points: Article 20(3): no person accused of an offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.
Article 20 gives three protections: ex post facto law, double jeopardy and self-incrimination.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Wrong: Article 24 fixes the age at 14, not 15.
Article 24 bans employing children below 14 in factories, mines and other hazardous work.
Wrong: Article 24 fixes the age at 14, not 16.
Age of adulthood/voting, not the Article 24 limit.

points: Article 24 is part of the Right against Exploitation (Articles 23–24).
Article 21A gives free and compulsory education to children aged 6–14 — the same 14-year line.
PYQ-POL-WEB-ACE09C.also: Article 24 is part of the Right against Exploitation (Articles 23–24).

PYQ-POL-WEB-AF19E6.lead: Indian judiciary is three-tier (option 3) and integrated.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Four-tier
No fourth tier exists in the regular court hierarchy.
Two-tier
Leaves out either the High Courts or the subordinate courts.
Three-tier
Supreme Court at top, High Courts in the middle, subordinate courts below.
Five-tier
Not the structure of the Indian judiciary.

points: A single integrated system enforces both Central and State laws, unlike the US double system.
This integrated system is taken from the Government of India Act, 1935.

PYQ-POL-WEB-BBA310.lead: The description of India is attributed to Carl Friedrich (option 1).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Carl Friedrich
German-American political scientist who wrote on constitutional government; the quote is attributed to him.
P.H. Appleby
American expert who wrote reports on Indian public administration (1953, 1956).
Woodrow Wilson
US President and early writer on public administration.
Jawaharlal Nehru
First Prime Minister; spoke of 'unity in diversity', not this description.

points: Friedrich wrote 'Constitutional Government and Democracy'; Laxmikanth quotes him on constitutionalism.
The quote stresses India's diversity of language and religion.

PYQ-POL-WEB-BC780D.lead: India's law-making process follows the British model (option 1).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: British Constitution
Gave parliamentary government, rule of law and legislative (law-making) procedure.
US Constitution
Gave Fundamental Rights and judicial review.
Irish Constitution
Ireland gave the Directive Principles, not the law-making process.
Canadian Constitution
Canada gave a federation with a strong Centre, not the law-making process.

points: Bills pass through readings in both Houses and get assent of the head of State — as in Westminster.
Britain also gave single citizenship, cabinet system and bicameralism.

PYQ-POL-WEB-C3257E.lead: Official key: option 3 (both 1 and 2). Strictly, only statement 1 is correct, so the study answer is option 1.

True/False
Why

True

Loosely true (official); strictly false

points: Option 2 fails because statement 1 is clearly true.
Option 4 fails because statement 1 is true.
Article 300 is in Part XII; Article 299 deals with government contracts.
PYQ-POL-WEB-C3257E.also: Disputed key: strictly, the legal name under Article 300 is 'Union of India', not 'Government of India', so only statement 1 is correct (option 1).

PYQ-POL-WEB-C6859B.lead: Part V (option 1) contains the Union Executive.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Part V
The Union — Executive (President, VP, PM, Council of Ministers), Parliament, Supreme Court, CAG (Articles 52–151).
Part III
Part III contains Fundamental Rights (Articles 12–35), not the Union Executive.
Part IV
Part IV contains Directive Principles (Articles 36–51), not the Union Executive.
Part VI
Part VI deals with the States (Articles 152–237), including the State Executive, not the Union.

points: Union Executive is in Chapter I of Part V (Articles 52–78).
Part VI is the mirror image for the States.

PYQ-POL-WEB-C8CD1C.lead: The Fourth Schedule deals with allocation of Rajya Sabha seats (option 2).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Administration of tribal areas
Wrong: tribal areas are dealt with in the Fifth and Sixth Schedules, not the Fourth.
Allocation of seats in the Council of States
Fourth Schedule — Rajya Sabha seats for States and UTs.
Union, State and Concurrent Lists
Wrong: the Union, State and Concurrent Lists are in the Seventh Schedule.
Recognised languages
Wrong: languages are listed in the Eighth Schedule.

points: It is linked to Articles 4 and 80.
Memory hook: 1st – States/UTs, 2nd – salaries, 3rd – oaths, 4th – Rajya Sabha seats.

PYQ-POL-WEB-D586E3.lead: The First Schedule (option 1) lists States and their territories.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: First
Names of States and Union Territories and their territories.
Second
Salaries, allowances of President, Governors, judges, CAG etc.
Third
The Third Schedule contains forms of oaths and affirmations, not the States and their territories.
Fourth
The Fourth Schedule allocates Rajya Sabha seats to States and UTs, not their names and territories.

points: It is linked to Articles 1 and 4.
Any new State or boundary change is made by amending the First Schedule.

PYQ-POL-WEB-D60F4C.lead: Delegated legislation means the legislature delegates rule-making to the executive (option 1).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?

Correct: Parliament passes the main law and lets the executive frame rules, regulations and bye-laws.
Executive delegates to legislature
Wrong direction: law-making power belongs to the legislature, so the executive cannot delegate it.

Not delegated legislation; the executive has no such legislative power to give.

PYQ-POL-WEB-D60F4C.also: Parliament checks it through Committees on Subordinate Legislation.

PYQ-POL-WEB-E74619.lead: Option 3 is the incorrect statement: KRMB's headquarters is not Chittoor.

PYQ-POL-WEB-E7AFE1.lead: Part III, Fundamental Rights (option 3), is called the Magna Carta of India.

What it is / means
Correct?

Part II deals with Citizenship (Articles 5–11), not with the rights called the Magna Carta.

Fundamental Rights — called the Magna Carta of India.

PYQ-POL-WEB-ECAAE8.lead: Severability keeps the valid part (option 3) and removes only the bad part.

What it is / means
Correct?

The part clashing with Fundamental Rights — this is struck out.

The constitutional part — this is retained.
Unconstitutional
The part violating the Constitution — this is struck out.

PYQ-POL-WEB-ECFC89.lead: The Seventh Schedule contains the three legislative lists (option 2).

What it is / means
Correct?

What it is / means
Correct?

PYQ-POL-00B238283058.lead: Liberty of occupation is not mentioned in the Preamble (option 4).

PYQ-POL-0552C459727C.lead: Political power in India lies with the people (option 3).

Correct?

PYQ-POL-06A24D04DD3F.lead: 'Sovereign' means India is not subject to any external authority (option 1).

PYQ-POL-0772F84A4742.lead: Liberty, equality and fraternity were taken from the French Revolution (option 2).

What it is / means
Correct?

What it is / means
Correct?

PYQ-POL-C5F57E94C7D9.lead: Official key: option 3 (B, C and D only). On the facts, only A and B describe Indian secularism, which is option 1.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: A. The State will have nothing to do with any religion
True
Broadly true as a test answer: India has no State religion and the State does not favour any religion; but Indian secularism is 'positive' — it treats all religions equally rather than ignoring them.
B. The State will not discriminate on grounds of religion
True
True: Articles 15 and 16 forbid discrimination on grounds of religion.
C. Christianity is the State religion
False
False: India has no official State religion; Article 28 bars religious instruction in fully State-funded schools.
D. No citizen will have any religion
False
False: Article 25 gives every person freedom of conscience and the right to profess, practise and propagate religion.

points: Option 2 (A, B, C) wrongly includes false statement C.
Option 3 (B, C, D) wrongly includes C and D and leaves out A — it cannot be right on the facts.
Option 4 (all) wrongly includes C and D.

PYQ-POL-C5F57E94C7D9.also: Disputed key: statements C and D are false, so option 3 cannot be correct; the best available answer is option 1 (A and B only).

PYQ-POL-D7BDD784459D.lead: Option 1: Liberty, Equality and Fraternity form the 'trinity' of the Preamble, taken from the French Revolution.

What it is / means
Correct?

Justice, Equality, Fraternity
Justice, Equality, Fraternity leaves out Liberty and wrongly includes Justice.

Socialism, Secularism, Democracy describe the nature of the Indian State, not the trinity of values.

points: LX p74: liberty, equality and fraternity were taken from the French Revolution (1789–1799).
Justice (social, economic, political) was taken from the Russian Revolution (1917).

Correct?

Equality of opportunity

Social justice
Social justice (no discrimination by caste, religion, sex) is only one half of distributive justice.
Economic justice

points: LX p74: 'A combination of social justice and economic justice denotes what is known as distributive justice'.
Indian socialism is 'democratic socialism' with a mixed economy, not State ownership of everything (LX p72).

PYQ-POL-DF6872C46B98.lead: Option 2: 'economic liberty' is not in the Preamble; 'economic' goes only with Justice.

Liberty of expression
Liberty of expression is one of the five liberties named in the Preamble.
Liberty of belief
Liberty of belief is one of the five liberties named in the Preamble.

points: The Preamble secures 'liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship' (LX p74).
Trap: do not mix the Justice clause with the Liberty clause.

PYQ-POL-E4FBC527828C.lead: Option 1: the ideal of Justice — social, economic and political — came from the Russian Revolution (1917).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?

Liberty of thought and expression is part of the Liberty ideal, which comes from the French Revolution.
Equality of status and of opportunity
Equality of status and of opportunity is part of the Equality ideal, also from the French Revolution.

points: LX p74: 'The ideal of justice—social, economic and political—has been taken from the Russian Revolution (1917).'
Memory hook: Russia = Justice (socialist ideal); France = Liberty-Equality-Fraternity.

PYQ-POL-FB06E994AC08.lead: All four statements are wrong, so none is valid: option 4.

True/False
Why

False

False

PYQ-POL-WEB-1F3FC2.lead: Option 4: the Preamble may be used to determine the ambit (scope) of Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.

Correct?

States demand

Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles
Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles: courts read them in the light of the Preamble's goals to decide their scope.

points: The Preamble is not enforceable, but courts use it to interpret provisions where the language is ambiguous (LX p76).

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. The Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution
True
True: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held it is part of the Constitution; LIC of India (1995) repeated this.
2. 'Secular' and 'socialist' were there since inception
False

points: Option 2 (2 only) picks the false statement and leaves out true statement 1.

PYQ-POL-WEB-8CF3D5.lead: Option 2: India has a parliamentary system — the executive comes from and is responsible to the legislature.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: unitary
Unitary describes Centre–State relations (all power with the Centre), not the type of executive; India is federal with a unitary bias.
parliamentary
Parliamentary: the PM and ministers are members of Parliament and collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Article 75(3)).
monarchical
Monarchical means a hereditary king or queen; India is a republic with an elected President.
presidential
Presidential (like the USA) means an executive independent of the legislature; India did not adopt it.

points: India took the parliamentary form from Britain; it exists at the Centre (Articles 74–75) and in States (Articles 163–164).
The President is only the nominal head; real power lies with the Council of Ministers.

What it is / means
Correct?

Rajendra Prasad was the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly; he did not move the Resolution.
JB Kripalani
J.B. Kripalani chaired the Fundamental Rights sub-committee; he did not move the Resolution.
Jawaharlal Nehru

PYQ-POL-WEB-C52DC6.lead: Option 4 is NOT correct: the Supreme Court does use the Preamble as an aid to interpretation where language is ambiguous.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: The term 'Secular Democratic Republic' was not there in the Preamble originally.
Correct statement: the original Preamble read 'Sovereign Democratic Republic'; 'Secular' was added in 1976.
The Preamble contains the basic structure of the Constitution of India.
Correct statement: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held the Preamble reflects the basic features of the Constitution.
By itself, the Preamble is not enforceable in a court of law.
Correct statement: the Preamble is non-justiciable — it cannot be enforced in court by itself.
The Supreme Court has held that the Preamble cannot be considered as an aid to the legal interpretation of the Constitution, where the language is ambiguous.
Not correct: courts refer to the Preamble to interpret ambiguous provisions, so this is the wrong statement and the answer.

points: LX p76: where terms in an article are ambiguous, the objectives in the Preamble help interpretation.
Trap: 'not enforceable' (true) is different from 'cannot be used to interpret' (false).

PYQ-POL-WEB-D69C22.lead: Option 3: every law must conform to the Constitution, which is the supreme law of the land.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Fundamental Right
Fundamental Rights: laws violating them are void (Article 13), but they are only one part of the Constitution.
Directive Principles
Directive Principles are non-justiciable goals (Part IV); a law is not struck down for not following them.
Constitution
Constitution: it is supreme; a law that violates any provision can be struck down by judicial review.
Preamble
Preamble: it is non-justiciable and is neither a source of power nor a limit on the legislature.

points: Judicial review lets courts declare any law that violates the Constitution void.
LX p76: the Preamble is neither a source of power to the legislature nor a prohibition upon its powers.

PYQ-POL-WEB-DC95BE.lead: Official key: option 4 — secularism protects everyone, including non-believers, so 'not applicable to irreligious persons' is not a component.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Equality incorporated in Article 14.
Equality under Article 14 is a core component: the State treats all persons equally, whatever their religion.
Prohibition against discrimination on ground of religion, caste, etc.
Prohibition of discrimination on religion, caste etc. (Articles 15, 16) is a core component of secularism.
Sentiments of the majority of people towards cow and against its slaughter
Not a component either: cow protection is in Article 48, a Directive Principle on agriculture and animal husbandry, not a part of secularism.
Not applicable to irreligious persons/citizen.
Not a component: Article 25 gives freedom of conscience to all persons, which includes the freedom not to follow any religion.

points: Secularism in India means equal respect and treatment for all religions and for non-believers (LX p73).
Article 25 protects 'all persons', so irreligious people are fully covered.
PYQ-POL-WEB-DC95BE.also: Disputed key: option 3 is also not a component of secularism, so the question has two correct 'except' answers; option 4 is the official key.

PYQ-POL-WEB-E83776.lead: Option 3 is NOT correct: the Preamble is not enforceable in a court of law.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: The words - Socialist and Secular, were not originally part of the Constitution
Correct statement: 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added in 1976 by the 42nd Amendment.
The Preamble states the objects of the Constitution of India
Correct statement: the Preamble states the objectives — justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
The Preamble is enforceable in a Court of Law
Not correct: the Preamble is non-justiciable, so this is the wrong statement and the answer.
A Republic refers to the people as the source of all authority under the Constitution
Correct statement: LX says a republic also means vesting political sovereignty in the people.

points: LX p76: the Preamble is non-justiciable and is neither a source of power nor a limit on the legislature.
LX p73: republic = elected head of State and sovereignty in the people.

PYQ-POL-WEB-F78D3D.lead: The incorrect statements are I and III: option 3.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: I. Preamble was enacted before the rest of the Constitution
False
Incorrect: LX says the Preamble was enacted after the rest of the Constitution, to keep it in line with it.
II. Part of the Constitution but no independent legal effect
True
Correct: it is part of the Constitution but cannot be enforced by itself.
III. It is enforceable through courts
False
Incorrect: the Preamble is non-justiciable.
IV. Nehru's Objectives Resolution became its foundation
True
Correct: the Resolution of 13 December 1946 was shaped into the Preamble.

points: The question asks for INCORRECT statements, so the answer is the False rows: I and III.
Option 1 (I, II) and option 4 (I, II, III) wrongly include the correct statement II.
Option 2 (II, IV) picks the two correct statements.

PYQ-POL-039070A84CAC.lead: Option 2: Ambedkar called the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) 'the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Freedom of Speech
Article 19(1)(a): freedom of speech and expression.
No — an important right, but not the one Ambedkar described this way.
Right to Constitutional Remedies
Article 32: right to move the Supreme Court to enforce FRs.
Right to Equality
Articles 14–18 form the Right to Equality.
No — an important right, but Ambedkar's 'heart and soul' words referred to Article 32.
Right to Religion
Articles 25–28: the Right to Freedom of Religion.
No — Ambedkar's 'heart and soul' words referred to Article 32, the remedy for all these rights.

points: Without a remedy, other rights would be empty promises; Article 32 makes all FRs enforceable (LX p144).
The Supreme Court has held Article 32 part of the basic structure.
PYQ-POL-039070A84CAC.also: The Supreme Court issues five writs: habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto.

PYQ-POL-03E2971D487C.lead: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so the answer is option 3 (1 and 3 only).

True/False

False

True
The Prime Minister's New 15-Point Programme (2006) is a welfare scheme for notified minorities.

Correct?

Article 14 uses 'any person', so it applies to citizens and foreigners alike.

What it is / means
Correct?

No — repugnancy is a Centre-State law concept, not a rule against double punishment.
Autrefois acquit

No — Article 20(2) needs punishment, so acquittal is not covered by it.
Autrefois convict

No — it is not a rule of criminal procedure, so it is not the basis of Article 20(2).

PYQ-POL-0AEFA6A0F40E.lead: Option 1: Fundamental Rights are mainly limits on the State, as defined in Article 12.

What it is / means
Correct?
rows: The State
Article 12: Government and Parliament, State governments and legislatures, local and other authorities.
Companies
Private bodies such as companies, which are not normally 'State'.
No — FRs generally do not bind private companies unless they are 'State'.
Women

No — women are holders of rights, not the party against whom they are claimed.

Educational institutions, which may be private or public.
No — only State-run or State-controlled ones count.

PYQ-POL-0AFD20E19A62.lead: Option 1 is the wrong statement, so it is the answer: freedom of religion is not unlimited.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Religion right without any limitations
✓ (the incorrect statement)
False. Article 25 is expressly 'subject to public order, morality and health' and to other provisions of Part III, and it is given to all persons, not only citizens.
2. No compulsion to pay taxes for promoting a religion
True. Article 27 says no person shall be compelled to pay taxes whose proceeds are used for promoting or maintaining any particular religion.
3. Religious instruction banned in State institutions
True. Article 28(1) bars religious instruction in institutions wholly maintained out of State funds (except those set up under an endowment or trust that requires it).
4. Not totally prohibited in non-State institutions
True. In State-recognised or State-aided institutions religious instruction may be given, but no one can be forced to attend it without consent (guardian's consent for a minor) — Article 28(3).

points: An 'except' question asks for the one false statement; only option 1 is false.
Restrictions on Article 25: public order, morality, health; the State may also regulate secular activities linked to religion and carry out social reform (LX p154-156).

PYQ-POL-0B0B373739C9.lead: Article 21A gives the Right to Education — free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Work
The right to work is a Directive Principle (Article 41), not a Fundamental Right, and it is not in Article 21A.
Privacy
Privacy was held to be part of Article 21 and Part III freedoms in Puttaswamy (2017); it has no separate article.
Equality
Equality before law is Article 14 (Right to Equality, Articles 14-18).
Education
Article 21A says the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of 6 to 14 years in the manner the State may by law determine.

points: Article 21A was inserted by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.
The RTE Act, 2009 gives effect to it; both came into force on 1 April 2010 (LX p150).
Memory hook: '21A' sits right after Article 21 because education is treated as part of a life with dignity.

PYQ-POL-0BA5C1494042.lead: Option 1: both prohibition and certiorari are supervisory writs that control lower courts and tribunals when they exceed or lack jurisdiction.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Both control inferior courts/tribunals exercising judicial or quasi-judicial functions
True. Both are 'jurisdictional writs' issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal; prohibition stops a case before the order, certiorari quashes the order after it.
2. Based on doctrine of equality
False. Equality (Article 14) has nothing to do with these writs; their basis is excess or lack of jurisdiction.
3. Available only in Supreme Court
False. Both the Supreme Court (Article 32) and the High Courts (Article 226) can issue all five writs.
4. Purely discretionary
False as the common feature. Under Article 32 the remedy is itself a Fundamental Right, so the Supreme Court cannot simply refuse; only Article 226 relief is discretionary.

points: Prohibition means 'to forbid' — it directs inactivity before the final order.
Certiorari means 'to be certified' — it quashes an order already passed (LX p160-161).
Prohibition is not available against administrative authorities; certiorari now is, where individual rights are affected.

PYQ-POL-0BC8AC97EC7E.lead: Habeas Corpus — the court examines whether a person's detention is legal.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Habeas Corpus
Means 'to have the body of'. The detainer must produce the person before the court, which checks the cause and legality of detention and frees him if it is illegal.
Certiorari
Means 'to be certified'. A higher court quashes an order already passed by a lower court or tribunal for excess or lack of jurisdiction.
Mandamus
Means 'we command'. It orders a public official or body to perform a duty it has failed or refused to perform.
Quo Warranto
Means 'by what authority'. It asks a person to show by what right he holds a public office.

points: The question's key word is 'detaining' — detention is tested only by habeas corpus.
Habeas corpus lies against public authorities and private persons; it is not issued where detention is lawful or ordered by a competent court (LX p160).

PYQ-POL-0BD6B872D2C7.lead: A writ under Article 32 cannot be used, because the right to property is no longer a Fundamental Right.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Writ under Article 226
Available. A High Court can issue writs for Fundamental Rights and 'for any other purpose', i.e. ordinary legal rights such as Article 300A.
Civil suit before a court
Available. A property dispute is an ordinary legal right that civil courts can decide.
Writ under Article 32
Not available. Article 32 can be used only to enforce Fundamental Rights; property is now a constitutional (legal) right under Article 300A.
Case before Lok Adalat
Available for settlement by compromise, like any civil dispute.

points: The 44th Amendment, 1978 deleted Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 and inserted Article 300A in Part XII (LX p164).
Article 32 needs violation of a Fundamental Right as its 'sine qua non' (LX p159).
PYQ-POL-0BD6B872D2C7.also: Article 300A: no person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law.

PYQ-POL-0C2D2AE86599.lead: Official key: Option 1 (Both true; R explains A). Settled law says A is false and R is true, an option not offered.

head: Part
True/False
Why
rows: A
False (doubtful as worded)
As a legal rule this is doubtful: courts cannot compel making a law.
R
True
Mandamus lies only to enforce existing policy.

points: Does R explain A? R states the real rule: mandamus enforces an existing duty or policy; it cannot force the Government or legislature to make a law. So R actually contradicts A instead of explaining it.
Official key is option 1 (both true, R explains A). On settled law A is false and R is true, but 'A false, R true' is not offered, so no option is strictly correct.
For exam purposes, remember the official key; for understanding, remember: no mandamus to make a law.
PYQ-POL-0C2D2AE86599.also: Disputed key: Assertion A is false (no mandamus lies to compel law-making) while R is true; 'A false, R true' is not among the options, so the official key 1 is doubtful.
PYQ-POL-0C2D2AE86599.better_answer: A is false, R is true (not offered); none of the four options is strictly correct.

PYQ-POL-0D74FAC42A45.lead: Parliament — only a law made by the legislature can restrict Fundamental Rights.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Parliament

Parliament (and State legislatures in their field) can make laws imposing reasonable restrictions, e.g. under Article 19(2)-(6); under Article 33 only Parliament can restrict rights of armed forces and police.
Prime Minister
The Prime Minister heads the executive; executive action cannot restrict a Fundamental Right without a law.
President
The President can only suspend enforcement of rights during a National Emergency (Article 359), not Articles 20 and 21; this is suspension, not the power to impose restrictions.
None of the above
Wrong, because Parliament does have this power.

points: Fundamental Rights 'are not absolute but qualified; the State can impose reasonable restrictions', and courts decide if they are reasonable (LX p129).
Article 33 power belongs only to Parliament, not State legislatures (LX p161).

PYQ-POL-101727413CC2.lead: Article 14 — equality before law and equal protection of laws.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Article 14
Heads the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18): the State shall not deny to any person equality before law or equal protection of laws.
Article 19
Gives citizens six freedoms: speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, profession.
Article 21
Protection of life and personal liberty.
Article 25
Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion.

points: 'Equality before law' (British idea) is a negative concept; 'equal protection of laws' (American idea) is a positive concept.
Articles 15-18: no discrimination, equal opportunity in public jobs, end of untouchability, abolition of titles (LX p128).

PYQ-POL-123E6E7D0AFF.lead: Article 24 prohibits employing children below 14 years in factories, mines and hazardous work.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Article 24
Bans employment of children below 14 in any factory, mine or other hazardous activity; part of the Right against Exploitation.
Article 19
Six freedoms of citizens; nothing on child labour.
Article 22
Protection against arrest and detention (rights of arrested persons, preventive detention).
Article 21
Article 21 protects life and personal liberty; it does not specifically deal with child labour in factories.

points: Article 23 (traffic, begar, forced labour) and Article 24 (child labour) together form the Right against Exploitation (LX p153-154).
The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 gives effect to Article 24.

PYQ-POL-16E5860AC91B.lead: Both prohibition and certiorari are issued against judicial and quasi-judicial authorities.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Executive authorities
Government organs that carry out laws; prohibition never lies against them.
Judicial and quasi-judicial authorities
Courts and bodies that decide disputes like courts (tribunals); both writs correct excess or lack of jurisdiction of such bodies.
Administrative authorities
Prohibition is not available against them; certiorari was later extended to them, so this is not common to both.
Legislative authorities
Neither writ lies against Parliament or State legislatures.

points: Prohibition is issued before the final order (stop the proceeding); certiorari after it (quash the order) (LX p161).
Both are called 'jurisdictional writs'.

PYQ-POL-185B3C593B68.lead: A and C are true, B and D are false: option 1 (A and C only).

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: A. Protected and enforced by the Constitution
True
Fundamental Rights are guaranteed by the Constitution and are justiciable — enforceable through Articles 32 and 226.
B. Amendable through normal legislative process
False
They can be curtailed only by a constitutional amendment under Article 368, not by an ordinary Act, and never against the basic structure.
C. Supreme Court is their guardian
True
The Supreme Court is the defender and guarantor of Fundamental Rights; a person can go to it directly under Article 32.
D. All constitutional rights are Fundamental Rights
False
Some rights are only constitutional rights outside Part III, e.g. property (Article 300A) and adult suffrage (Article 326).

points: Option 2 wrongly includes B and leaves out C.
Option 3 wrongly includes B.
Option 4 wrongly includes D (LX p127-129).

PYQ-POL-18C7600BC95D.lead: Official key: option 2. Study answer: option 3 — Article 32 can be amended by a special (two-thirds) majority under Article 368, but not so as to destroy it.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Simple majority
Simple majority is used only for provisions outside Article 368 (e.g. new States, Article 2-4); Fundamental Rights are not amended this way.
Cannot be amended
✗ (official key)
Article 32 is part of the basic structure, so its core cannot be destroyed; but no Part III article is wholly beyond amendment.
Two-thirds majority
✓ (study answer)
Part III is amended by special majority: majority of total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting in each House.
Ratification by the States
State ratification is needed only for federal provisions listed in Article 368(2); Article 32 is not in that list.

points: Fundamental Rights 'can be curtailed only by a constitutional amendment act and not by an ordinary act', without touching basic structure (LX p129).
The examiner probably chose 'cannot be amended' because Article 32 is basic structure; students should know both points.
PYQ-POL-18C7600BC95D.also: Disputed key: official key is option 2 (cannot be amended); constitutionally, Article 32 can be amended by special majority under Article 368 within the basic-structure limit, so the study answer is option 3.

PYQ-POL-18D475361A02.lead: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 removed property from the list of Fundamental Rights.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 26th Amendment
1971: abolished privy purses and privileges of former rulers.
42nd Amendment
1976: added 'socialist, secular, integrity' to the Preamble and Fundamental Duties (Part IVA).
44th Amendment
1978: deleted Articles 19(1)(f) and 31, and inserted Article 300A in Part XII making property a legal right.
43rd Amendment
1977: reversed some 42nd Amendment changes (e.g. restored jurisdiction of courts); did not touch property.

points: Right to property is still a constitutional right, but not part of the basic structure (LX p164).
Memory hook: 44th undid the Emergency excesses — and also moved property out of Part III.

PYQ-POL-1A4215A99E82.lead: Section 66A was struck down in 2015 for violating freedom of speech and expression, Article 19(1)(a).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Right to Information
RTI is read into Article 19(1)(a) and given by the RTI Act, 2005, but it was not the issue in Shreya Singhal.
Freedom of speech and expression
Section 66A punished online messages that were 'grossly offensive' or caused 'annoyance'; these vague words went beyond the grounds in Article 19(2).
Right to practise any trade or occupation
That is Article 19(1)(g); the case was about speech, not business.
Right to education
Right to education is Article 21A; it was not involved in Shreya Singhal, which was about online speech.

points: A restriction on speech is valid only if it fits one of the eight grounds in Article 19(2) and is reasonable.
'Annoyance' or 'inconvenience' is not such a ground, so the section was void (Shreya Singhal v. Union of India, 24 March 2015).

PYQ-POL-1C5BC4EB237E.lead: Article 20(2) — no person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Article 19
Article 19 gives six freedoms to citizens; it does not deal with double jeopardy.
Article 20
Protection in respect of conviction for offences: no ex-post-facto criminal law (20(1)), no double jeopardy (20(2)), no self-incrimination (20(3)).
Article 21
Article 21 protects life and personal liberty; the bar on double punishment is in Article 20(2).
Article 22
Safeguards against arrest and detention.

points: Double jeopardy protection applies only to proceedings before a court of law or judicial tribunal, not to departmental proceedings (LX p147).
Article 20 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.

PYQ-POL-1D1E778E1B42.lead: Sedition is not a ground in Article 19(2).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Sedition
Not listed in Article 19(2); sedition-type speech can be restricted only if it falls under 'security of the State' or 'public order'.
Incitement to an offence
Listed ground in Article 19(2) (added by the 1st Amendment, 1951).
Contempt of court
Contempt of court is expressly listed as a ground of restriction in Article 19(2), so it is not the answer.
Friendly relations with foreign States
Listed ground (added by the 1st Amendment, 1951).

points: Eight grounds of Article 19(2): sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, decency or morality, contempt of court, defamation, incitement to an offence (LX p142).
Memory hook: 'Sedition' was dropped from the draft Article on purpose by the Constituent Assembly.

PYQ-POL-1D6B7F3FE06A.lead: There are six groups of Fundamental Rights at present.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Original number in 1950, including the right to property (Article 31).
Eight groups was never the number in Part III; there were seven originally and six now.
Equality, Freedom, Against exploitation, Religion, Cultural and educational, Constitutional remedies.
Too few; all six groups are still in Part III.

points: The 44th Amendment, 1978 removed the right to property, reducing seven to six (LX p127).
Property is now a legal right under Article 300A, Part XII.

PYQ-POL-1EC454D260F9.lead: Haryana — its 75% private-job quota law for local residents was struck down by the Punjab and Haryana High Court in November 2023.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Karnataka
Has proposed local-quota bills, but none was struck down as asked here.
Jharkhand
Passed a local-employment law (2021), but it is not the law struck down.
Andhra Pradesh
