LX-PQ-003.lead: Option 4: the Estimates Committee has all 30 members from the Lok Sabha only.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Committee on Assurances
Wrong: each House has its own Committee on Government Assurances (15 in Lok Sabha, 10 in Rajya Sabha).
2. Committee on Delegated Legislation
Wrong: each House has its own Committee on Subordinate (Delegated) Legislation, 15 members each.
3. Committee on Public Undertakings
Wrong: the Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 members, 15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha.
4. Estimates Committee
Correct: the Estimates Committee is purely a Lok Sabha committee of 30 members; the Rajya Sabha has no representation.

points: The PAC also has Rajya Sabha members (15 + 7).
Memory hook: 'Estimates' and the Lower House — both decide money.
LX-PQ-003.also: PAC (15 LS + 7 RS) and COPU (15 LS + 7 RS) include Rajya Sabha members.

LX-PQ-121.lead: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are Estimates Committee functions, so the answer is option 2.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: To suggest alternative policies to bring efficiency and economy in administration.
True
The Estimates Committee may suggest alternative policies to bring efficiency and economy in administration.
To see that expenditure conforms to the authority which governs it.
False
This is a Public Accounts Committee function, which checks spending after it is done.
To examine whether money is well laid out within the policy implied in the estimates.
True
The Estimates Committee examines whether money is well laid out within the policy limits.
To suggest the form in which estimates shall be presented to Parliament.
True
The Estimates Committee suggests the form in which the estimates are presented to Parliament.

points: Options 1, 3 and 4 wrongly include statement 2, which is a PAC duty; option 1 also omits 3 and 4.
It is called a 'continuous economy committee'.
LX-PQ-121.also: Estimates Committee is called a 'continuous economy committee'.

LX-PQ-143.lead: Option 3: Lanka Sundaram first visualised a separate committee on public undertakings in 1953.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Ashok Mehta
Wrong: Ashok Mehta is known for the 1977 committee on Panchayati Raj, not this idea.
2. G.V. Mavalankar
Wrong: G.V. Mavalankar was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha; he did not first propose this committee.
3. Lanka Sundaram
Correct: Lanka Sundaram, an MP, first raised the need for a separate committee on public undertakings.
4. Krishna Menon Committee
Wrong: the Krishna Menon Committee recommended setting it up later, leading to COPU in 1964, but it did not first visualise it.

points: COPU began in 1964 with 15 members, raised to 22 (15 LS + 7 RS) in 1974.

LX-PQ-157.lead: Option 4: excess grants must first be approved by the Public Accounts Committee before Lok Sabha votes on them.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Additional grant
Wrong: an additional grant is for a new service not in the budget, and does not need PAC approval.
2. Exceptional grant
Wrong: an exceptional grant is for a special purpose outside the current service, and is voted directly.
3. Token grant
Wrong: a token grant is a small sum voted when the money is found by reappropriation.
4. Excess grant
Correct: an excess grant covers money already spent beyond the grant; because it is past spending, the PAC examines it first.

points: This links with the PAC's role of checking spending after it is done.

POL-724-AR-01.lead: Option 1: a consultative committee is not a parliamentary committee because it lacks House appointment, direction by the presiding officer, reporting to the House and a parliamentary secretariat.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. It may not satisfy the institutional conditions of appointment, direction, reporting and secretariat support

Correct: a parliamentary committee is appointed or elected by the House, works under the presiding officer, reports to the House and has a parliamentary secretariat; consultative committees meet none of these.
2. MPs may never serve on committees
Wrong: MPs do serve on many committees, including consultative committees.
3. Only constitutional bodies are committees
Wrong: most parliamentary committees are not constitutional bodies; they are created by House rules.
4. Every committee must examine expenditure
Wrong: only financial committees examine expenditure; many others, like Privileges, do not.

points: Consultative committees are formed by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs and are informal discussion forums.

POL-724-AR-02.lead: Option 1: a Select Committee has members of one House, while a Joint Committee has members of both Houses.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. A Select Committee belongs to one House; a Joint Committee includes both Houses
Correct: this is the basic difference between the two types of committee on Bills.
2. Only a Select Committee may examine clauses
Wrong: both types examine a Bill clause by clause.
3. A Joint Committee cannot receive expert evidence
Wrong: both may take expert and public evidence.
4. Both are permanent financial committees
Wrong: both are ad hoc committees on Bills that end after reporting, not permanent financial committees.

points: Memory hook: 'Select' = single House, 'Joint' = joined Houses.

POL-724-CH-01.lead: Option 1: an inquiry JPC is ad hoc; it is set up for one specific matter and ends after it reports.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. An inquiry JPC is ad hoc for a specific assigned matter
Correct: JPCs are formed by a motion of Parliament for a given inquiry, like Bofors (1987) or 2G spectrum (2011).
2. A JPC is constitutionally permanent
Wrong: a JPC is not created by the Constitution, and it is not permanent.
3. Standing committees dissolve after every report
Wrong: standing committees are permanent and continue between reports.
4. A JPC cannot include Rajya Sabha members
Wrong: a JPC includes members of both Houses, including the Rajya Sabha.

points: Standing committees are permanent; ad hoc committees end when their task is done.

POL-724-CH-02.lead: Option 1: the PAC checks spending already done, using CAG reports, while the Estimates Committee studies budget estimates and suggests economies through the year.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. PAC scrutinises expenditure, accounts and CAG findings; Estimates Committee studies estimates, economy and efficiency and may work through the financial year
Correct: both are financial standing committees but look at different stages: PAC after spending, Estimates before.
2. Both committees certify Money Bills
Wrong: only the Speaker certifies Money Bills.
3. PAC frames delegated legislation; Estimates Committee hears petitions
Wrong: delegated legislation is checked by the Subordinate Legislation Committee, and petitions go to the Petitions Committee.
4. Both are ad hoc inquiry committees
Wrong: PAC and Estimates are standing committees, not ad hoc ones.

points: Memory hook: PAC = post-mortem; Estimates = pre-planning.

POL-724-P243-01.lead: Option 2: the Public Accounts Committee examines the CAG's audit reports on government spending.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Estimates Committee
Wrong: the Estimates Committee studies budget estimates before spending, not audit reports.
2. Public Accounts Committee
Correct: the PAC examines the CAG's reports on appropriation and finance accounts.
3. Business Advisory Committee
Wrong: the Business Advisory Committee fixes time for House business.
4. Rules Committee
Wrong: the Rules Committee considers matters of procedure in the House.

points: The CAG is called the 'friend, philosopher and guide' of the PAC.
PAC has 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS).
POL-724-P243-01.also: PAC: 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS); its chair is by convention from the Opposition.

POL-724-P244-01.lead: Option 1: the Estimates Committee suggests economies and alternative policies in administration.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Estimates Committee
Correct: it reports what economies, improvements and alternative policies can be adopted within the estimates.
2. Public Accounts Committee
Wrong: the PAC checks spending already done, not alternative policies.
3. Privileges Committee
Wrong: the Privileges Committee examines breach of privilege of the House and its members.
4. Petitions Committee
Wrong: the Petitions Committee examines petitions from the public.

points: It is called a 'continuous economy committee'.
It has 30 members, all from Lok Sabha.

POL-724-P245-01.lead: Option 1: the Committee on Public Undertakings examines reports and accounts of public enterprises.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Committee on Public Undertakings
Correct: COPU examines reports, accounts and CAG reports on public undertakings.
2. Estimates Committee
Wrong: the Estimates Committee studies ministries' budget estimates.
3. Ethics Committee
Wrong: the Ethics Committee deals with members' conduct.
4. General Purposes Committee
Wrong: the General Purposes Committee advises on matters affecting the House that do not fall under any other committee.

points: COPU was set up in 1964 and has 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS).

POL-724-P246-01.lead: Option 1: the Committee on Subordinate Legislation checks whether rules made by the executive stay within the powers given by Parliament.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Committee on Subordinate Legislation
Correct: it examines whether powers to make rules, regulations and bye-laws are properly exercised.
2. Committee on Petitions
Wrong: the Committee on Petitions examines petitions from citizens.
3. Library Committee
Wrong: the Library Committee looks after the Parliament library.
4. House Committee
Wrong: the House Committee deals with members' housing and amenities.

points: 'Subordinate legislation' means rules made by government under powers delegated by an Act.

POL-724-P248-01.lead: All three statements are true, so the answer is option 4.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: Demands for grants.
True
DRSCs examine demands for grants of their ministries before they are voted by the Lok Sabha.
Referred bills.
True
DRSCs examine bills referred to them by the Speaker or the Chairman.
Annual reports.
True
DRSCs examine the annual reports of their ministries or departments.

points: Options 1, 2 and 3 each leave out at least one true function.
DRSCs also examine long-term policy documents referred to them.

POL-724-P249-01.lead: Option 2: parliamentary committee recommendations are advisory.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Judicially enforceable
Wrong: courts cannot enforce committee recommendations.
2. Advisory
Correct: committees advise; the government may accept or reject their recommendations.
3. Constitutional amendments
Wrong: committees cannot amend the Constitution; that needs Article 368.
4. Binding money decrees
Wrong: committees cannot issue binding money orders.

points: Governments usually accept many recommendations, so committees still carry weight.

POL-724-REC-STAGE-001.lead: Option 1: the Ethics Committee examines misconduct of members and recommends action.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Ethics Committee
Correct: it enforces the code of conduct of MPs.
2. Business Advisory Committee
Wrong: the Business Advisory Committee fixes time for House business.
3. Committee on Petitions
Wrong: the Committee on Petitions examines petitions from citizens.
4. Committee on Government Assurances
Wrong: the Committee on Government Assurances checks whether ministers kept their promises in the House.

points: Rajya Sabha set up its Ethics Committee in 1997 and Lok Sabha in 2000.

POL-R21-COM-assurances-subleg-structure.lead: Option 2: each House has its own committees; Assurances has 15 LS and 10 RS members, and Subordinate Legislation has 15 in each House.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Both are joint committees of 30 members elected by the two Houses
Wrong: these are not joint committees, and their members are nominated, not elected.
2. Each House has its own committee; Assurances has 15 Lok Sabha and 10 Rajya Sabha members, while Subordinate Legislation has 15 in each House
Correct: Assurances has 15 members in Lok Sabha and 10 in Rajya Sabha, while Subordinate Legislation has 15 members in each House.
3. Assurances exists only in Lok Sabha, while Subordinate Legislation exists only in Rajya Sabha
Wrong: both committees exist in both Houses.
4. Both have 22 members, including 15 from Lok Sabha and seven from Rajya Sabha
Wrong: 22 members (15 + 7) is the size of PAC and COPU.

points: Both were constituted in 1953.

POL-R21-COM-constitutional-references.lead: Both statements are true, so the answer is option 4.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: Article 88 lets Ministers and the Attorney-General take part in a committee they are named members of, but gives no right to vote.
True
Article 88 gives the right to speak and take part, but not to vote.
The Constitution does not provide a full composition-and-tenure code for ordinary committees.
True
Details come from House Rules of Procedure, made under Article 118.

points: Options 1 and 2 each leave out a true statement; option 3 rejects both.
POL-R21-COM-constitutional-references.also: Committees draw authority from Articles 105 and 118 and the House Rules.

POL-R21-COM-consultative-arrangements.lead: Option 4: the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs constitutes Consultative Committees of MPs from both Houses for each ministry, and the minister presides.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. The Prime Minister’s Office creates committees of Lok Sabha members only to issue binding directions to ministries
Wrong: they include MPs of both Houses and cannot issue binding directions.
2. The Speaker appoints judges to committees chaired by the Chief Justice for executive audit
Wrong: no judges or Chief Justice are involved.
3. The President forms permanent committees of Rajya Sabha members only, independently of ministries
Wrong: they include both Houses and are tied to ministries.

4. The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs constitutes committees of MPs from both Houses for ministries/departments, initially after the new Lok Sabha; the concerned minister normally presides over informal policy-and-working discussions
Correct: they are formed after a new Lok Sabha and provide informal discussions between ministers and MPs.

points: Membership is voluntary and depends on the choice of members.

POL-R21-COM-functional-families.lead: Petitions/Privileges/Ethics inquire; Assurances etc. scrutinise; Rules/Business Advisory etc. run day-to-day business; General Purposes/House/Library serve — option 3 (1–2–3–4).

head: List-I
Correct match (List-II)
Why / concept
rows: A. Petitions, Privileges, Ethics
1. Inquiry
They inquire into complaints, breaches and conduct.
B. Assurances, Subordinate Legislation, SC/ST, Women, Profit
2. Scrutiny and control
These committees watch over the executive (assurances, delegated rules, SC/ST and women's welfare, offices of profit), so they belong to the scrutiny-and-control group.
C. Rules, Absence, Private Members, Business Advisory
3. Day-to-day business
These committees deal with procedure, members' leave and the timetable of business, helping the House run its day-to-day sittings.
D. General Purposes, House, Library, Salaries
4. Housekeeping/service
These committees provide facilities and services to members (accommodation, library, salaries), so they are housekeeping committees.

points: Option 1 (1–3–2–4) is wrong: it gives B→3 (Day-to-day business); C→2 (Scrutiny and control).
Option 2 (2–1–3–4) is wrong: it gives A→2 (Scrutiny and control); B→1 (Inquiry).
Option 4 (4–2–3–1) is wrong: it gives A→4 (Housekeeping/service); D→1 (Inquiry).

POL-R21-COM-joint-composition.lead: SC/ST Welfare and Empowerment of Women each have 20 LS + 10 RS; the Library Committee has 6 LS + 3 RS — option 4 (A–1, B–1, C–2).

head: List-I
Correct match (List-II)
Why / concept
rows: A. Welfare of SCs and STs
The Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs is a joint committee with 20 Lok Sabha and 10 Rajya Sabha members, so A matches 1.
B. Empowerment of Women
The Committee on Empowerment of Women follows the same joint pattern as the SC/ST committee, 20 Lok Sabha plus 10 Rajya Sabha members, so B also matches 1.
C. Library
The Library Committee is a small house-keeping joint committee of 6 Lok Sabha and 3 Rajya Sabha members, so C matches 2.

points: Code 1 can be used twice; no committee here has 10 + 5.
Option 1 (A–1, B–3, C–2) is wrong: it gives B→3 (10 + 5 — fits none of these).
Option 2 (A–3, B–1, C–2) is wrong: it gives A→3 (10 + 5 — fits none of these).
Option 3 (A–1, B–2, C–3) is wrong: it gives B→2 (6 + 3); C→3 (10 + 5 — fits none of these).

POL-R21-COM-offices-profit-structure.lead: Option 3: the Joint Committee on Offices of Profit has 15 members (10 LS + 5 RS) and recommends on offices.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Joint Committee on Offices of Profit: 30 members(20 LS+10 RS), ending automatically after one year.
Wrong: the committee has 15 members and lasts for the term of the Lok Sabha.
2. Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances: 15 members(10 LS+5 RS), finally deciding all MP disqualifications.
Wrong: the Salaries Committee frames salary rules; it does not decide disqualifications.
3. Joint Committee on Offices of Profit: 15 members(10 LS+5 RS), functioning till Lok Sabha dissolution and making recommendations on offices.
Correct: it examines committees and other bodies appointed by the government and recommends whether their offices should disqualify an MP.
4. Committee of Privileges: 15 LSmembers, amending the Constitution to exempt every government office.
Wrong: the Privileges Committee examines breach of privilege and cannot amend the Constitution.

points: The final decision on disqualification lies with the President, on the Election Commission's opinion (Article 103).

POL-R21-COM-ordinary-membership-patterns.lead: Business Advisory 15/11; Petitions 15/10; Privileges 15/10; Rules 15/16 — option 1 (A–2, B–1, C–1, D–3).

head: List-I
Correct match (List-II)
Why / concept
rows: A. Business Advisory
Each House has its own Business Advisory Committee: 15 members in the Lok Sabha and 11 in the Rajya Sabha, so A matches 2.
B. Petitions
Each House has a separate Committee on Petitions: 15 members in the Lok Sabha and 10 in the Rajya Sabha, so B matches 1.
C. Privileges
Each House has its own Committee of Privileges, with 15 Lok Sabha and 10 Rajya Sabha members, the same pattern as Petitions, so C matches 1.
D. Rules
Each House has its own Rules Committee: 15 members in the Lok Sabha and 16 in the Rajya Sabha, so D matches 3.

points: Code 1 appears twice.
Option 2 (A–1, B–2, C–1, D–3) is wrong: it gives A→1 (15 / 10); B→2 (15 LS / 11 RS).
Option 3 (A–2, B–3, C–1, D–1) is wrong: it gives B→3 (15 / 16); D→1 (15 / 10).
Option 4 (A–3, B–1, C–2, D–1) is wrong: it gives A→3 (15 / 16); C→2 (15 LS / 11 RS); D→1 (15 / 10).

POL-R21-COM-quorum-subcommittee.lead: Option 1: the quorum is one-third (10 of 30); the committee may form a subcommittee, whose report becomes the committee's report only after full committee approval.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Quorum is 10; it may form a subcommittee, and that subcommittee’s report needs approval at a sitting of the whole committee to become its report
Correct: under the general Lok Sabha committee rules, quorum is about one-third of members, and a subcommittee's report needs approval of the whole committee.
2. Quorum is 3; every subcommittee report automatically binds the House
Wrong: the quorum is not 3, and no subcommittee report automatically binds the House.
3. Quorum is 15; subcommittees are forbidden
Wrong: the quorum is not 15, and subcommittees are allowed.
4. Quorum is 10; the subcommittee may replace the whole committee without approval
Wrong: the subcommittee cannot replace the whole committee without approval.

points: No committee report binds the House automatically.

POL-R21-COM-salaries-statutory-structure.lead: Option 3: the Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances is constituted under the 1954 Act and has 15 members (10 LS + 5 RS).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. A constitutional body set up under Article 106 and chaired by the Speaker
Wrong: it is a statutory body, not constitutional, and not chaired by the Speaker.
2. A financial committee of 30 members elected only by the Lok Sabha
Wrong: it is not a financial committee and not elected only by Lok Sabha.
3. A committee constituted under the Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954, with 10 Lok Sabha and 5 Rajya Sabha members
Correct: it frames rules for salary, allowances and pension of MPs.
4. An ad hoc committee appointed by the Ministry of Finance after every general election
Wrong: it is not appointed by the Ministry of Finance.

points: Article 106 lets Parliament fix MPs' salaries by law.

POL-R21-COM-specific-functions.lead: Petitions suggest remedies, Privileges examine breaches, Assurances check ministers' promises, Rules review procedure — option 1 (A–3, B–1, C–4, D–2).

head: List-I
Correct match (List-II)
Why / concept
rows: A. Petitions
3. Examines petitions, suggests remedies
The Committee on Petitions examines petitions from the public on their grievances and suggests remedies, so A matches 3.
B. Privileges
1. Breach-of-privilege matters
The Committee of Privileges examines cases of breach of privilege of the House or its members, a quasi-judicial role, so B matches 1.
C. Government Assurances
4. Ministers' assurances fulfilled
The Committee on Government Assurances checks whether promises and undertakings given by ministers on the floor of the House have been fulfilled, so C matches 4.
D. Rules
2. Reviews procedure rules
The Rules Committee considers matters of procedure and conduct of business in the House and recommends amendments to the rules, so D matches 2.

points: Option 2 (A–1, B–3, C–4, D–2) is wrong: it gives A→1 (Breach-of-privilege matters); B→3 (Examines petitions, suggests remedies).
Option 3 (A–3, B–4, C–2, D–1) is wrong: it gives B→4 (Ministers' assurances fulfilled); C→2 (Reviews procedure rules); D→1 (Breach-of-privilege matters).
Option 4 (A–4, B–1, C–3, D–2) is wrong: it gives A→4 (Ministers' assurances fulfilled); C→3 (Examines petitions, suggests remedies).

POL-R21-COM-standing-adhoc-continuity.lead: Option 2: X is a standing committee; Y is ad hoc.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Both must be ad hoc because their members can change
Wrong: membership change does not make a committee ad hoc.
2. X is standing; Y is ad hoc
Correct: standing committees are permanent; ad hoc committees end after their task.
3. X is ad hoc; Y is standing
Wrong: this reverses the definitions; an enduring, regularly reconstituted committee is standing, and a task-specific one is ad hoc.
4. Both must be standing because they report to Parliament
Wrong: reporting to Parliament does not decide the type.

points: Example: PAC is standing; a Select Committee on a Bill is ad hoc.
POL-R21-COM-standing-adhoc-continuity.also: Examples: PAC is standing; a Select Committee on a Bill is ad hoc.

POL-R21-COM-welfare-service-functions.lead: SC/ST Welfare reviews safeguards, Women reviews NCW reports, Library advises on library, Absence handles leave — option 2 (A–3, B–4, C–1, D–2).

head: List-I
Correct match (List-II)
Why / concept
rows: A. SC/ST safeguards
3. SC/ST Welfare
The Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs reviews how the constitutional safeguards for SCs and STs are working, so A matches 3.
B. NCW reports
4. Empowerment of Women
The Committee on Empowerment of Women examines matters such as NCW reports and measures for women's equality, so B matches 4.
C. Library improvement
1. Library
Improving the library is the work of the Library Committee, a house-keeping committee, so C matches 1.
D. Leave applications
2. Absence
Leave applications from members are examined by the Committee on Absence of Members, so D matches 2.

points: Option 1 (A–4, B–3, C–1, D–2) is wrong: it gives A→4 (Empowerment of Women); B→3 (SC/ST Welfare).
Option 3 (A–3, B–4, C–2, D–1) is wrong: it gives C→2 (Absence); D→1 (Library).
Option 4 (A–2, B–4, C–1, D–3) is wrong: it gives A→2 (Absence); D→3 (SC/ST Welfare).

POL-R21-COPU-business-boundary.lead: Option 3: COPU checks whether undertakings follow sound business principles without running them.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. It replaces the undertaking’s managers and approves each routine purchase order.
Wrong: COPU does not take over management or approve purchase orders.
2. It examines only whether a ministry has issued enough delegated rules.
Wrong: delegated rules are the Subordinate Legislation Committee's work.
3. It scrutinises sound business principles and prudent commercial practices without taking over day-to-day administration.
Correct: COPU examines whether affairs are managed in accordance with sound business principles and prudent commercial practices.
4. It conducts no commercial scrutiny because a public undertaking is autonomous.
Wrong: autonomy does not exempt undertakings from parliamentary scrutiny.

points: COPU does not examine major government policy or day-to-day administration.

POL-R21-COPU-remit-boundaries.lead: Only statement 1 is true, so the answer is option 1.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: It examines the reports and accounts of public undertakings and CAG reports on them.
True
This is COPU's main function: it examines the reports and accounts of public undertakings and the CAG's reports on them.
It can examine major government policy as distinct from business functions.
False
COPU is barred from examining major government policy and day-to-day administration.

points: Option 2 wrongly includes false statement 2; option 3 rejects true statement 1; option 4 includes both.

POL-R21-DRSC-constitution.lead: Option 2: a DRSC has up to 31 members: 21 nominated by the Speaker and 10 by the Chairman; ministers are ineligible; the term is one year.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. 31 members: 20 from Lok Sabha and 11 from Rajya Sabha, with ministers eligible for membership
Wrong: it is 21 + 10, and ministers are barred.
2. Up to 31 members: 21 nominated by the Lok Sabha Speaker and 10 by the Rajya Sabha Chairman; ministers are ineligible, and the term does not exceed one year
Correct: each DRSC has 31 members (21 Lok Sabha nominated by the Speaker, 10 Rajya Sabha by the Chairman), ministers cannot be members, and the term is one year.
3. 30 members directly elected by all MPs for a fixed five-year term
Wrong: members are nominated, not elected, and the term is one year.
4. 31 members nominated entirely by the President, including the minister whose department is examined
Wrong: the Speaker and the Chairman nominate members, not the President.

points: A member who becomes minister ceases to be a member.

POL-R21-DRSC-history-distribution.lead: Option 1: 17 DRSCs were set up in 1993 and raised to 24 in 2004; 16 work under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. 1993: 17 committees; 2004: 24 committees; 16 under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha
Correct: DRSCs began in 1993 with 17 committees, and seven more in 2004 made 24, of which 16 are serviced by the Lok Sabha and 8 by the Rajya Sabha secretariat.
2. 1993: 24 committees; 2004: 17 committees; 16 under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha
Wrong: the years are reversed; there were 17 DRSCs in 1993, raised to 24 in 2004, not the other way round.
3. 1993: 17 committees; 2004: 24 committees; 8 under the Lok Sabha and 16 under the Rajya Sabha
Wrong: the split between the Houses is reversed.
4. 1993: 17 committees; 2004: 31 committees; 21 under the Lok Sabha and 10 under the Rajya Sabha
Wrong: 31 is the number of members in each DRSC, not the number of committees.

points: Seven more committees were added in 2004.

POL-R21-DRSC-longterm-policy.lead: Option 4: DRSCs may examine national basic long-term policy documents referred by the Speaker or Chairman.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Every individual transfer order of departmental staff as routine day-to-day administration
Wrong: they do not consider day-to-day administration.
2. A cut motion imposed by the committee directly on Lok Sabha
Wrong: they cannot move cut motions or bind the House.
3. Any private commercial document without a parliamentary referral
Wrong: they examine only matters referred under the rules.
4. National basic long-term policy documents presented to the Houses and referred by the Speaker or Rajya Sabha Chairman
Correct: DRSCs examine national basic long-term policy documents presented to the Houses when the Speaker or Chairman refers them.

points: Their other functions are demands for grants, bills and annual reports.

POL-R21-EST-continuous-selected-review.lead: Option 4: the Estimates Committee may continue its examination through the year and need not examine every estimate before grants are voted.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. It must examine the entire estimates each year, and no demand for grants may be voted before its report.
Wrong: it examines selected estimates, and voting does not wait for its report.
2. It submits every report only to Rajya Sabha and gives binding daily spending directions.
Wrong: it reports to Lok Sabha, and its advice is not binding.
3. It examines only matters allotted to COPU and never reviews departmental estimates.
Wrong: departmental estimates are its core work.
4. It may continue examination through the financial year, report to Lok Sabha as it proceeds, and need not examine every estimate before grants are voted.
Correct: it examines selected ministries each year.

points: It is called a 'continuous economy committee'.

POL-R21-EST-specific-functions.lead: Option 3: the Estimates Committee recommends improvements, checks allocations against policy and suggests the form of estimates.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Adjudicate an individual election petition and award compensation
Wrong: election petitions go to High Courts.
2. Allocate time for debate and certify a Money Bill
Wrong: Business Advisory allots time; the Speaker certifies Money Bills.
3. Recommend organisational and administrative improvements consistent with the estimates’ policy, check whether allocations serve that policy, and suggest the form of presenting estimates
Correct: the Estimates Committee reports on improvements in organisation and administration, checks whether money is well laid out within the policy, and suggests the form of estimates.
4. Conduct the CAG’s statutory audit and issue binding directions to spend money
Wrong: audit is the CAG's job; committees issue no binding orders.

points: It suggests economies and alternative policies.

POL-R21-FIN-LS-election-term.lead: Option 3: Lok Sabha elects members by proportional representation using STV; membership term is one year.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. President nominates them for five years
Wrong: the House elects them, not the President.
2. Speaker appoints all of them for three years with compulsory one-third rotation
Wrong: the Speaker does not appoint the members, and there is no three-year term or compulsory rotation rule.
3. Lok Sabha elects them by proportional representation using STV; membership term does not exceed one year
Correct: the Lok Sabha members of PAC, Estimates and COPU are elected every year by proportional representation with single transferable vote, so the term does not exceed one year.
4. Members are selected by a simple lottery for an unrestricted term
Wrong: members are elected by the House, and the one-year term is fixed, so a lottery and an unlimited term are both invented.

points: The Speaker appoints only the chairperson.
POL-R21-FIN-LS-election-term.also: Speaker appoints only the chairperson, not the members.

POL-R21-FIN-REMAIN-BAC-constitution.lead: Option 2: in each House the presiding officer nominates the Business Advisory Committee (BAC) and is its chairman.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Members are elected by both Houses jointly, and the Finance Minister chairs both BACs
Wrong: the two BACs are separate committees of each House, not jointly elected, and the Finance Minister has no role; the Speaker chairs the Lok Sabha BAC and the Chairman chairs the Rajya Sabha BAC.
2. Each presiding officer nominates and chairs that House’s BAC; Lok Sabha’s serves for the Speaker-specified period or until replacement, and Rajya Sabha’s until a new BAC is nominated

Correct: the Speaker nominates and chairs the Lok Sabha BAC (15 members) and the Chairman nominates and chairs the Rajya Sabha BAC (11 members); the Rajya Sabha body continues until a new BAC is nominated.
3. The President nominates both BACs, which have a fixed five-year term regardless of reconstitution
Wrong: the President has no role in House committees, and no committee of Parliament has a fixed five-year term; BACs are reconstituted by the presiding officers.
4. Each BAC elects an outside expert as chair, and its membership ends after every time-allocation report
Wrong: no outsider can chair a parliamentary committee; the BAC is a standing committee whose membership does not end after each report.

points: The BAC fixes the programme and timetable of the House and allots time to government business.
In Rajya Sabha the BAC also does the work of allotting time to private members' bills, since Rajya Sabha has no separate Private Members' Committee.
Memory hook: BAC = the House's timetable maker, headed by the House's own head.

POL-R21-FIN-REMAIN-BAC-time-role.lead: Option 3: the Business Advisory Committee recommends how much time each stage of a Bill should get.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Public Accounts Committee
Wrong: the PAC examines the CAG's audit reports on spending already made; it does not plan House time.
2. Committee on Petitions
Wrong: the Committee on Petitions examines petitions on bills and on matters of public importance; it does not fix timetables.
3. Business Advisory Committee

Correct: the BAC regulates the programme and timetable of the House and allocates time for government legislative and other business; once the House agrees to its report, the time allocation takes effect.
4. Committee on Public Undertakings
Wrong: the Committee on Public Undertakings examines the reports and accounts of public sector undertakings, not House business.

points: Lok Sabha BAC: 15 members with the Speaker as chairman; Rajya Sabha BAC: 11 members with the Chairman as ex-officio chairman.
It belongs to the group 'committees relating to the day-to-day business of the House'.

POL-R21-FIN-REMAIN-PAC-chair-20261103.lead: Option 4: K. C. Venugopal (Congress, Opposition) has chaired the PAC in the 18th Lok Sabha since 2024 and was reappointed by Speaker Om Birla for 2026–27.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Sanjay Jaiswal
Wrong: Sanjay Jaiswal (BJP) has headed the Estimates Committee in the 18th Lok Sabha, not the PAC; the Estimates chair is generally from the ruling side.
2. Baijayant Panda
Wrong: Baijayant Panda (BJP) has been associated with chairing the Committee on Public Undertakings, not the PAC.
3. Shashi Tharoor
Wrong: Shashi Tharoor (Congress) has chaired the Standing Committee on External Affairs, a department-related standing committee, not the PAC.
4. K. C. Venugopal
Correct: K. C. Venugopal was appointed PAC chairman in 2024 and reappointed when the financial committees were reconstituted for 2026–27 (May 2026).

points: By a convention since 1967, the PAC chairman is taken from the Opposition; the Speaker appoints him from among the committee's members.
This explains why an Opposition leader, not a ruling-party MP, heads the PAC.

POL-R21-FIN-REMAIN-Petitions-chair.lead: Option 1: the Speaker appoints the Deputy Speaker as chair of Lok Sabha's Committee on Petitions (because he is a member), while the Rajya Sabha Chairman appoints its chair from among the committee's members.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Lok Sabha’s Speaker appoints the Deputy Speaker as committee chair; Rajya Sabha’s Chairman appoints its chair from committee members

Correct: under Lok Sabha rules, if the Deputy Speaker is a member of a committee he must be appointed its chairman; in Rajya Sabha, where the Deputy Chairman is not a member, the Chairman picks the chair from the members.
2. Both committees elect an outside expert as chair
Wrong: a parliamentary committee's chair is always an MP who is a member of the committee, never an outside expert.
3. The President appoints both chairs, without regard to committee membership
Wrong: the President has no role in appointing chairs of House committees; committees work under the direction of the Speaker/Chairman.
4. The Prime Minister appoints the Lok Sabha chair and the Finance Minister appoints the Rajya Sabha chair
Wrong: ministers, including the Prime Minister and Finance Minister, have no power over House committees, which exist to check the executive.

points: Committee on Petitions: 15 members in Lok Sabha, 10 in Rajya Sabha.
A parliamentary committee is appointed or nominated by the House or the presiding officer and works under the presiding officer's direction.

POL-R21-FIN-REMAIN-RS-election-method.lead: Option 3: Rajya Sabha chooses its members for the PAC and COPU by proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote (PR-STV).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Direct election by all adult voters in the State
Wrong: committee members are MPs chosen inside Parliament; ordinary voters elect MPs, not committee members.
2. A simple lottery among eligible members
Wrong: no lottery is used; a contested choice is settled by a vote of the House.
3. Proportional representation by the single transferable vote
Correct: PAC and COPU members are elected every year by PR-STV, so that all parties get fair representation; Rajya Sabha elects 7 members to each.
4. Appointment by the President without a House election
Wrong: the President does not appoint committee members; the House itself elects them.

points: PAC = 22 (15 LS + 7 RS); COPU = 22 (15 LS + 7 RS); both elected by PR-STV for one year.
The Estimates Committee has no Rajya Sabha members at all (30, all from Lok Sabha).

POL-R21-FIN-REMAIN-classification.lead: Option 4: the PAC, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings are the three financial committees.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Public Accounts; Petitions; Business Advisory
Wrong: the PAC is financial, but the Committee on Petitions is a committee to inquire and the BAC is a committee on day-to-day business of the House.
2. Estimates; Rules; Privileges
Wrong: the Estimates Committee is financial, but the Rules Committee deals with House procedure and the Committee of Privileges is a committee to inquire.
3. Public Undertakings; Government Assurances; Ethics
Wrong: COPU is financial, but Government Assurances is a committee to scrutinise and control and Ethics is a committee to inquire.
4. Public Accounts; Estimates; Public Undertakings
Correct: Laxmikanth lists exactly three financial committees — Public Accounts, Estimates and Public Undertakings.

points: Six groups of standing committees: financial, DRSCs, to inquire, to scrutinise and control, day-to-day business, and house-keeping.
Memory hook: 'PEC' — Public Accounts, Estimates, COPU = money committees.

POL-R21-FIN-REMAIN-financial-description.lead: Option 1: the PAC (1921) is the oldest financial committee, and the Estimates Committee is called the 'continuous economy committee'.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Public Accounts Committee; Estimates Committee
Correct: the PAC was set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919; the Estimates Committee suggests economies in the budget estimates, hence 'continuous economy committee'.
2. Estimates Committee; Public Accounts Committee
Wrong: this reverses the pair; the Estimates Committee (post-independence 1950) is younger than the PAC, and the PAC does audit review, not economy suggestions.
3. Committee on Public Undertakings; Estimates Committee
Wrong: COPU (1964) is the youngest of the three, not the oldest.
4. Public Accounts Committee; Committee on Public Undertakings
Wrong: the PAC part is right, but COPU examines public undertakings; the 'economy' title belongs to the Estimates Committee.

points: PAC 1921 → Estimates 1950 (on John Mathai's recommendation) → COPU 1964 (Krishna Menon Committee).
The Estimates Committee is the largest: 30 members, all from Lok Sabha.

POL-R21-FIN-REMAIN-historical-expansion.lead: Option 3: the Estimates Committee grew from 25 to 30 members in 1956(–57), and COPU grew from 15 to 22 members in 1974.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Estimates: 15 to 22 in 1974; COPU: 25 to 30 in 1956–57
Wrong: the numbers are swapped between the committees; 15 to 22 belongs to COPU and the Estimates Committee never had 15 members.
2. Estimates: 25 to 30 in 1974; COPU: 15 to 22 in 1956–57
Wrong: both numbers are right but the years are swapped; the Estimates increase came in 1956, the COPU increase in 1974.
3. Estimates: 25 to 30 from 1956–57; COPU: 15 to 22 in 1974
Correct: the Estimates Committee began in 1950 with 25 members, raised to 30 in 1956; COPU began in 1964 with 15 (10 LS + 5 RS), raised to 22 (15 LS + 7 RS) in 1974.
4. Estimates: 30 to 25 from 1956–57; COPU: 22 to 15 in 1974
Wrong: it reverses the direction; both committees were enlarged, not reduced.

points: Hook: Estimates 25→30 (1956); COPU 15→22 (1974).

POL-R21-FIN-composition.lead: Option 2: PAC and COPU each have 15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha members, while the Estimates Committee has 30 Lok Sabha members only.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. PAC: 30 Lok Sabha members; Estimates: 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha; COPU: 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha
Wrong: it gives the PAC the Estimates Committee's 30-LS-only pattern; the PAC actually has 22 members including 7 from Rajya Sabha.
2. PAC: 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha; Estimates: 30 Lok Sabha members; COPU: 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha
Correct: PAC = 15 LS + 7 RS; Estimates = 30 LS, with no Rajya Sabha representation; COPU = 15 LS + 7 RS.
3. PAC: 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha; Estimates: 20 Lok Sabha and 10 Rajya Sabha; COPU: 30 Lok Sabha members
Wrong: the Estimates Committee has no Rajya Sabha members, and COPU is not 30-LS-only.
4. PAC: 10 Lok Sabha and 5 Rajya Sabha; Estimates: 30 Rajya Sabha members; COPU: 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha
Wrong: 10 + 5 was COPU's original strength (1964), not the PAC's; and the Estimates Committee is entirely Lok Sabha, not Rajya Sabha.

points: The Estimates Committee is all-Lok Sabha because estimates and grants are voted only by Lok Sabha.
All three are elected every year by PR-STV for a one-year term.

POL-R21-FIN-ministers-chairs.lead: Option 2: a member who becomes a minister ceases to be a member, and the Speaker appoints the chairman from among the committee's members.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Membership continues automatically; the President appoints the chair
Wrong on both: membership does not continue (a minister cannot be a member), and the President has no role in naming the chair.
2. Membership ceases; the Speaker appoints the chair from the committee’s members
Correct: a minister cannot be elected to the PAC, Estimates Committee or COPU, and one who becomes a minister ceases to be a member; the chairman is appointed by the Speaker from among the members.
3. Only voting rights cease; the Prime Minister appoints the chair
Wrong on both: the whole membership ends, not just voting rights, and the Prime Minister does not appoint committee chairs.
4. Membership ceases only after a court order; the Finance Minister appoints the chair
Wrong on both: no court order is needed, as the cessation is automatic under the rules; and the Finance Minister has no role.

points: Reason: these committees examine the executive's spending, so a minister (part of the executive) cannot sit in judgment on his own government.
Even for Rajya Sabha members of PAC/COPU, the chairman is chosen by the Lok Sabha Speaker.

POL-R21-FIN-origins.lead: PAC 1921, Estimates 1950 (John Mathai), COPU 1964 (Krishna Menon Committee) — option 2 (1–2–3).

head: List-I
Correct match (List-II)
Why / concept
rows: A. PAC
The Public Accounts Committee was first set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919, so A matches 1.
B. Estimates Committee
2. 1950, John Mathai
The first post-Independence Estimates Committee was set up in 1950 on the recommendation of Finance Minister John Mathai, so B matches 2.
C. COPU
3. 1964, Krishna Menon Committee
The Committee on Public Undertakings was set up in 1964 on the recommendation of the Krishna Menon Committee to examine public sector undertakings, so C matches 3.

points: Option 1 (1–3–2) is wrong: it gives B→3 (1964, Krishna Menon Committee); C→2 (1950, John Mathai).
Option 3 (2–1–3) is wrong: it gives A→2 (1950, John Mathai); B→1 (1921).
Option 4 (3–2–1) is wrong: it gives A→3 (1964, Krishna Menon Committee); C→1 (1921).

POL-R21-JE-JPC-food-law-causal-qualifica.lead: The JPC urged faster completion of an integrated food law already in progress.

head: No.

Authority already established
Wrong — came later, 2006 Act

points: The Food Safety and Standards Act was passed in 2006; FSSAI was set up in 2008.

POL-R21-JE-JPC-market-disclosure-effect.lead: SEBI amended disclosure guidelines considering both the JPC and the Malegam Committee.

head: No.
Option
Verdict
rows: No amendment
Wrong — guidelines were amended
Amended, after JPC and Malegam

Only Malegam

points: SEBI circular of 2 May 2003 recorded these amendments.

POL-R21-JE-JPC-pesticide-finding-limits.lead: Option 4: the 2003 JPC chaired by Sharad Pawar inquired into pesticide residues in soft drinks, fruit juices and other beverages.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Adulteration of milk and edible oils
Wrong: milk and edible oil adulteration was not the subject of a JPC; food adulteration is dealt with under food safety law.
2. Field trials of genetically modified crops
Wrong: GM crop field trials were examined by the Standing Committee on Agriculture, not a 2003 JPC.
3. Spurious drugs in government hospitals
Wrong: no JPC was set up on spurious drugs in hospitals; drug quality is a matter for drug regulators.
4. Pesticide residues in soft drinks and other beverages
Correct: after reports of pesticide residues in cola drinks (2003), a JPC under Sharad Pawar examined the issue and recommended safety standards for such beverages.

points: Inquiry JPCs are ad hoc: they are created for one matter and end when they report.
Major inquiry JPCs: Bofors 1987, Harshad Mehta 1992, Ketan Parekh 2001, soft drinks 2003, 2G 2011.

POL-R21-JPC-LS-motion-dates.lead: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, so option 1 ('1 and 2 only') is the answer.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. Its terms of reference and membership are laid down in the motion by which it is constituted.
True
An inquiry JPC is an ad hoc committee created by a motion adopted in one House and agreed to by the other; that motion fixes its subject, membership and time limit.
2. It can take oral and written evidence and call for documents.
True
Like other parliamentary committees, a JPC can examine witnesses, take written memoranda and call for records relating to the matter under inquiry.
3. Its recommendations are binding on the Government.
False
Committee recommendations are only advisory; the Government may accept or reject them, and only Parliament takes final decisions.

points: Option 2 (2 and 3) and option 3 (1 and 3) both wrongly include statement 3.
Option 4 (all three) fails for the same reason — binding recommendations do not exist for parliamentary committees.

POL-R21-JPC-Securities-government-respon.lead: Option 2: the coal block allocation was NOT inquired into by a JPC; it was exposed by the CAG and examined through the PAC and the courts.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Bofors contract
Wrong choice: the Bofors gun contract was the subject of the first inquiry JPC (1987, chaired by B. Shankaranand).
2. Allocation of coal blocks
Correct: the coal block allocation controversy came from a CAG report (2012), was taken up by the PAC and finally decided by the Supreme Court (2014); no JPC was formed.
3. Pesticide residues in soft drinks
Wrong choice: pesticide residues in soft drinks were examined by a JPC in 2003 under Sharad Pawar.
4. Allocation of 2G spectrum
Wrong choice: 2G spectrum allocation was examined by a JPC set up in 2011 under P. C. Chacko.

points: In a 'NOT' question, three options are real JPCs; find the odd one out.
Hook: Coal went to CAG–PAC–Court, not a JPC.

POL-R21-JPC-Telecom-membership.lead: Option 4: the 2011 telecom (2G) JPC had 30 members — 20 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. 30 members: 15 from Lok Sabha and 15 from Rajya Sabha
Wrong: JPCs do not give equal seats to both Houses; Lok Sabha usually gets twice the Rajya Sabha share.
2. 40 members: 30 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha
Wrong: the total was 30, not 40, and the split was not 30 + 10.
3. 20 members: 10 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha
Wrong: the total was 30, not 20, and the Houses were not equally represented.
4. 30 members: 20 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha
Correct: the JPC set up in 2011 to examine telecom licences and spectrum pricing had 30 members in the 2:1 ratio (20 LS + 10 RS), chaired by P. C. Chacko.

points: The 2:1 pattern matches other joint committees, e.g. the SC/ST Welfare Committee and Committee on Empowerment of Women (20 + 10).

POL-R21-JPC-constitution-sittings.lead: Stock Market JPC: 27 Apr 2001, 105 sittings; Pesticide JPC: 22 Aug 2003, 17 sittings.

head: JPC
Constituted
Sittings
rows: Stock Market
105 (incl. sub-committees)
Pesticide residues

points: 26 April 2001 was the date of the motions, not formal constitution.

POL-R21-JPC-formal-constitution.lead: Option 3: the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024 was referred in August 2024 to a Joint Committee of both Houses chaired by Jagdambika Pal.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. The Department-related Standing Committee on Social Justice and Empowerment
Wrong: it was not sent to a DRSC; the House adopted a motion to send it to a Joint Committee.
2. A Select Committee of the Rajya Sabha
Wrong: a Select Committee has members of one House only; this Bill went to a committee of both Houses.
3. A Joint Committee of both Houses chaired by Jagdambika Pal
Correct: Lok Sabha referred the Bill to a Joint Committee of 31 members of both Houses under Jagdambika Pal; after its report the Bill was passed and became law in April 2025.
4. The Public Accounts Committee
Wrong: the PAC examines CAG audit reports on spending; it never examines Bills.

points: A Bill can be referred by motion to a Select Committee (one House) or a Joint Committee (both Houses), which examines it clause by clause.
So a 'JPC' can be on a Bill (advisory) as well as for an inquiry into a scandal.

POL-R21-JPC-sittings-presentation.lead: Option 4: the first inquiry JPC (1987) was on the Bofors gun contract, chaired by B. Shankaranand.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Irregularities in securities and banking transactions (Harshad Mehta)
Wrong: the Harshad Mehta securities and banking JPC came later, in 1992.
2. The stock market scam (Ketan Parekh)
Wrong: the Ketan Parekh stock market JPC was set up in 2001.
3. Allocation of 2G spectrum
Wrong: the 2G spectrum JPC was set up in 2011.
4. The Bofors gun contract
Correct: the Bofors JPC of 1987 was the first JPC set up to inquire into an alleged scandal.

points: Order to remember: Bofors 1987 → Harshad Mehta 1992 → Ketan Parekh 2001 → soft drinks 2003 → 2G 2011.

POL-R21-JPC-three-chairs-parties.lead: Option 2: P. C. Chacko chaired the 2011 2G spectrum JPC.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Murli Manohar Joshi
Wrong: Murli Manohar Joshi was then chairman of the PAC, which examined the 2G issue separately through the CAG report.
2. P. C. Chacko
Correct: P. C. Chacko (Congress) chaired the JPC on allocation and pricing of telecom licences and spectrum, set up in 2011.
3. Sharad Pawar
Wrong: Sharad Pawar chaired the 2003 JPC on pesticide residues in soft drinks.
4. Ram Niwas Mirdha
Wrong: Ram Niwas Mirdha chaired the 1992 JPC on the Harshad Mehta securities scam.

points: Hook: 'Chacko–2G', 'Pawar–Pepsi/Cola', 'Mirdha–Mehta'.

POL-R21-JPC-two-historical-profiles.lead: Option 1: 2–4–3–1 = Bofors (1987), Harshad Mehta (1992), Ketan Parekh (2001), 2G (2011).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Correct: this follows the dates 1987 → 1992 → 2001 → 2011.
Wrong: it puts Ketan Parekh (2001) before Harshad Mehta (1992).
Wrong: it puts Harshad Mehta (1992) before Bofors (1987), the very first inquiry JPC.
Wrong: it puts 2G (2011) before Ketan Parekh (2001).

points: Trick: the two stock-market scams go 'H before K' — Harshad Mehta (1992) before Ketan Parekh (2001).

POL-R21-ORD-absence-ls.lead: Option 3: only Lok Sabha has a Committee on Absence of Members, with 15 members.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Both Houses jointly; 30
Wrong: it is not a joint committee and does not have 30 members.
2. Rajya Sabha only; 10
Wrong: Rajya Sabha has no such committee; there such leave matters are dealt with by the House itself.
3. Lok Sabha only; 15
Correct: it is a special committee of Lok Sabha with 15 members that considers leave applications and cases of members absent for 60 days or more without permission.
4. Each House separately; 22
Wrong: the committee exists only in Lok Sabha, and 22 is the size of PAC/COPU.

points: Article 101(4): a House may declare a member's seat vacant if he is absent for 60 days without its permission.
Similar Lok Sabha-only committee: Private Members' Bills and Resolutions.

POL-R21-ORD-chairs-appointment.lead: Option 3: the presiding officer of each House nominates its Privileges and Subordinate Legislation Committees, and the Speaker/Chairman is ex-officio chairman of that House's Rules Committee.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Each House elects its Privileges and Subordinate Legislation Committee members by the single transferable vote; its presiding officer is ex officio chair of the Rules Committee
Wrong: these committees are nominated, not elected by STV; STV election is used for the financial committees.
2. Each House’s presiding officer nominates its Privileges and Subordinate Legislation Committee members; the Deputy Speaker or Deputy Chairman is ex officio chair of its Rules Committee
Wrong: the Rules Committee is chaired by the Speaker (LS) or Chairman (RS) himself, not by the deputy.
3. Each House’s presiding officer nominates its Privileges and Subordinate Legislation Committee members; the Speaker or Chairman is ex officio chair of its respective Rules Committee
Correct: both committees are nominated by the presiding officer; the Rules Committee has the Speaker (15 members, LS) or Chairman (16 members, RS) as ex-officio chairman.
4. The Lok Sabha Speaker nominates both Houses’ Privileges and Subordinate Legislation Committee members and is ex officio chair of both Rules Committees
Wrong: each House runs its own committees; the Lok Sabha Speaker has no power over Rajya Sabha committees.

points: The Rules Committee recommends amendments to the rules of procedure of the House.
Privileges Committee: 15 members (LS), 10 (RS); Subordinate Legislation: 15 in both Houses.

POL-R21-ORD-drsc-recommendation-purpose.lead: Option 4: DRSCs (1993) were set up on the Lok Sabha Rules Committee's recommendation to secure greater accountability of the executive, especially financial, and better budget debate.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Public Accounts Committee recommendation; closer executive and financial accountability through budget scrutiny
Wrong: the PAC did not recommend the DRSCs; it examines CAG audit reports.
2. Lok Sabha Rules Committee recommendation; replacing the Houses’ budget decisions with binding committee decisions
Wrong: the body is right, but DRSCs do not replace House decisions; their reports are advisory and the House still votes the demands.
3. Estimates Committee recommendation; closer executive and financial accountability through budget scrutiny
Wrong: the purpose is right, but the recommendation came from the Rules Committee, not the Estimates Committee.
4. Lok Sabha Rules Committee recommendation, developed through both Houses’ committee and rules process; closer executive and financial accountability and better-informed budget scrutiny

Correct: 17 DRSCs were set up in 1993 on the Lok Sabha Rules Committee's recommendation, aimed at executive (financial) accountability and more informed budget scrutiny; 7 more came in 2004, making 24.

points: Each DRSC has 31 members (21 LS + 10 RS), nominated by the presiding officers; 16 work under Lok Sabha and 8 under Rajya Sabha.
They examine demands for grants before they are voted, but cannot suggest cut motions.

POL-R21-ORD-ethics-origins.lead: Option 1: the Ethics Committee was constituted in Rajya Sabha in 1997 and in Lok Sabha in 2000.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Rajya Sabha: 1997; Lok Sabha: 2000
Correct: Rajya Sabha set up its Ethics Committee in 1997; Lok Sabha followed in 2000 (ad hoc at first, permanent from 2015).
2. Rajya Sabha: 2000; Lok Sabha: 1997
Wrong: it swaps the years; Rajya Sabha came first.
3. Both Houses: 1993
Wrong: 1993 is the year the DRSC system started, not the Ethics Committees.
4. Rajya Sabha: 1989; Lok Sabha: 1997
Wrong: 1989 is when the first three subject committees (forerunners of DRSCs) were set up, not an Ethics Committee.

points: The Ethics Committee enforces the code of conduct of MPs and examines cases of misconduct.
Lok Sabha Ethics Committee: 15 members; Rajya Sabha: 10.

POL-R21-ORD-ethics-standing-term.lead: Option 3: Lok Sabha's Ethics Committee is now a standing committee under the Lok Sabha Rules, nominated by the Speaker, with a term not exceeding one year.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. An ad hoc committee nominated by the Speaker, continuing until its assigned task is completed
Wrong: it was ad hoc only at the beginning (2000); since 2015 it has been a permanent standing committee under the Rules.
2. A standing committee elected by Lok Sabha through proportional representation by the single transferable vote, for a term not exceeding one year
Wrong: its members are nominated by the Speaker, not elected by PR-STV.
3. A standing committee under the Lok Sabha Rules, nominated by the Speaker, for a term not exceeding one year
Correct: rules added in 2015 made it a standing committee of 15 members nominated by the Speaker, holding office for not more than one year.
4. A standing committee nominated by the Speaker, continuing until Lok Sabha is dissolved
Wrong: its term is up to one year, not the full life of Lok Sabha.

points: It enforces the MPs' code of conduct; a complaint from a non-member must come through an MP.
Remember: 'nominated + one year' is the common pattern for most non-financial standing committees of Lok Sabha.

POL-R21-ORD-general-purposes.lead: Option 2: each House has its own General Purposes Committee, chaired ex officio by its presiding officer, dealing with House matters not covered by any other committee.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. A joint committee of both Houses, chaired by the Lok Sabha Speaker, including deputies and standing committee chairs, dealing with residual House affairs
Wrong: it is not a joint committee; each House has its own.
2. A separate committee in each House, with its presiding officer as ex officio chair and members including the deputy and standing committee chairs, dealing with residual House affairs

Correct: members include the presiding officer as chairman, the Deputy Speaker/Deputy Chairman, panel of chairpersons, chairpersons of departmental standing committees and leaders of parties; it advises on residual affairs of the House.
3. A separate committee in each House, with its deputy presiding officer as ex officio chair and members including standing committee chairs, dealing with residual House affairs
Wrong: the deputy presiding officer is a member, but the chair is the Speaker/Chairman.
4. A separate committee in each House, chaired by its presiding officer and including the deputy and standing committee chairs, principally examining government expenditure through audit reports
Wrong: the composition is right, but examining audit reports is the PAC's work, not this committee's.

points: It is a house-keeping (service) committee, along with the House Committee and Library Committee.

POL-R21-ORD-inquiry-jpc-routes.lead: Option 1: a joint inquiry can be set up by a motion adopted in one House and concurred in by the other, or by the two presiding officers acting together.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. A motion adopted by one House and concurred in by the other; or the two presiding officers acting in consultation with each other
Correct: Laxmikanth says inquiry committees are constituted either by the two Houses on a motion, or by the Speaker/Chairman; for a joint body both Houses (or both presiding officers) must agree.
2. A motion adopted by one House without the other House’s concurrence; or the two presiding officers acting in consultation with each other
Wrong: a joint committee needs the other House's concurrence, because it includes that House's members.
3. A motion adopted by one House and concurred in by the other; or either presiding officer acting alone for both Houses
Wrong: one presiding officer cannot act for both Houses; each controls only its own House.
4. A recommendation by a committee of one House without further parliamentary action; or a minister’s order following consultation with the presiding officers
Wrong: a committee recommendation or a minister's order cannot create a parliamentary committee; only the Houses or presiding officers can.

points: Inquiry JPCs are ad hoc and end when they submit their report.

POL-R21-ORD-inquiry-jpc-subject.lead: Option 2: an investigative JPC is formed of members of both Houses to inquire into a specific public controversy within its terms of reference.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Members of Lok Sabha examining the clauses of a bill referred to a Select Committee
Wrong: this is a Select Committee of one House examining a Bill clause by clause.
2. Members of both Houses inquiring into a specified public controversy, such as alleged large-scale financial irregularities, within the terms assigned to the committee
Correct: an inquiry JPC (e.g. Bofors, 2G) has members of both Houses and investigates a specific matter, not a Bill.
3. Members of both Houses examining only the clauses of a bill referred to a Joint Committee
Wrong: this is a Joint Committee on a Bill — both Houses, but its job is legislative scrutiny, not investigation.
4. Members of a standing financial committee routinely examining audit reports within its continuing remit
Wrong: this is the routine work of a standing financial committee like the PAC, which is permanent, not ad hoc.

points: Ad hoc committees are of two kinds: inquiry committees and advisory committees (select/joint committees on Bills).

POL-R21-ORD-ls-assurances-subleg.lead: Option 1: for both the Government Assurances and Subordinate Legislation Committees, the Speaker nominates members, ministers are ineligible, and the term does not exceed one year.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. The Speaker nominates the members; ministers are ineligible; the term does not exceed one year
Correct: both are Lok Sabha committees nominated by the Speaker (15 members each), ministers cannot be nominated, and the term is up to one year.
2. Lok Sabha elects the members by proportional representation through the single transferable vote; ministers are ineligible; the term does not exceed one year
Wrong: PR-STV election is for the financial committees; these two are nominated.
3. The Speaker nominates the members; ministers are eligible; the term does not exceed one year
Wrong: ministers are not eligible, because the Assurances Committee checks ministers' own promises and the other checks executive rule-making.
4. The Speaker nominates the members; ministers are ineligible; the committees continue until Lok Sabha is dissolved
Wrong: their term is up to one year, not until dissolution.

points: Government Assurances: checks promises made by ministers on the floor of the House (constituted 1953).
Subordinate Legislation: checks rules made by the executive under delegated powers (constituted 1953).

POL-R21-ORD-official-language-election.lead: Option 4: the Committee of Parliament on Official Language has 30 members — 20 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha — elected by PR-STV.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. 30 members: 20 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha, elected by the respective Houses by simple majority
Wrong: the numbers are right, but election is by PR-STV, not simple majority.
2. 30 members: 15 from each House, elected by the respective Houses through proportional representation by the single transferable vote
Wrong: the committee is 20 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha, not 15 from each House.
3. 30 members: 20 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha, nominated by the respective presiding officers
Wrong: members are elected by the Houses, not nominated by the presiding officers.
4. 30 members: 20 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha, elected by the respective Houses through proportional representation by the single transferable vote
Correct: section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 provides 30 members (20 LS + 10 RS) elected by each House by PR-STV.

points: The committee reviews progress in the use of Hindi for official purposes and reports to the President (Article 344 also provides a similar committee of 30 members).

POL-R21-ORD-private-bills.lead: Option 2: it is a Lok Sabha committee of 15 members with the Deputy Speaker as chairman, term not exceeding one year.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. A Lok Sabha committee, normally of 15 members, chaired by the Speaker for a term not exceeding one year; it classifies private members’ bills and recommends discussion time
Wrong: the Deputy Speaker, not the Speaker, chairs this committee.
2. A Lok Sabha committee, normally of 15 members including the Deputy Speaker as chair, for a term not exceeding one year; it classifies private members’ bills and recommends discussion time
Correct: Laxmikanth calls it a special committee of Lok Sabha of 15 members including the Deputy Speaker as chairman; it classifies private members' bills and allots time for them and resolutions.
3. A joint committee of 20 Lok Sabha and 10 Rajya Sabha members, chaired by the Deputy Speaker for one year; it classifies private members’ bills and recommends discussion time
Wrong: it is not a joint committee; Rajya Sabha has no such committee and its BAC does this work.
4. A Lok Sabha committee, normally of 15 members including the Deputy Speaker as chair, continuing until Lok Sabha is dissolved; it classifies private members’ bills and recommends discussion time
Wrong: its term is up to one year, not until dissolution.

points: Private member = any MP who is not a minister.

POL-R21-ORD-privileges-semi-judicial.lead: Option 2: the Committee of Privileges performs semi-judicial functions.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Committee on Petitions
Wrong: the Petitions Committee examines petitions and representations; it is grievance-related, not judicial.
2. Committee of Privileges
Correct: it examines cases of breach of privilege of the House and its members, hears evidence like a court, and recommends action.
3. Committee on Government Assurances
Wrong: the Government Assurances Committee checks whether ministers' promises are fulfilled.
4. Rules Committee
Wrong: the Rules Committee recommends changes in procedural rules.

points: 'Semi-judicial' because it weighs evidence and recommends punishment, though the House makes the final decision.
Privileges: 15 members (LS), 10 (RS).

POL-R21-ORD-rs-continuity.lead: Option 3: these Rajya Sabha committees hold office until a new committee is nominated.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Each committee automatically ceases one year after nomination, even if no replacement committee has been nominated
Wrong: they do not lapse automatically after one year if no successor is nominated.
2. Each committee automatically ceases at the end of every parliamentary session
Wrong: they do not end with each session; they work between sessions too.
3. Each committee holds office until a new committee is nominated; periodic reconstitution does not guarantee permanent individual membership
Correct: Rajya Sabha is a permanent House, so its committees continue until replaced; reconstitution may change individual members.
4. Each committee’s term is coextensive with Lok Sabha and ends when Lok Sabha is dissolved
Wrong: Rajya Sabha is never dissolved, so its committees are not linked to Lok Sabha's term.

points: Contrast: most Lok Sabha committees have a term not exceeding one year.

POL-R21-ORD-salaries-rules.lead: Rules need Central Government consultation, both presiding officers' confirmation and Gazette publication.

head: No.
Option
Verdict
rows: Consult; both confirm; Gazette
Correct
Gazette alone enough
Wrong — confirmation needed
No consultation
Wrong — consultation needed
Speaker alone confirms
Wrong — both confirm

points: Act: Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954.

POL-R21-ORD-scst-election-term.lead: Option 4: each House elects its members by PR-STV, and the term does not exceed one year.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Members are nominated by the respective presiding officers; the term does not exceed one year
Wrong: members are elected, not nominated.
2. Members are elected by the respective Houses through proportional representation by the single transferable vote; the term lasts until Lok Sabha is dissolved
Wrong: the election part is right, but the term is up to one year, not till dissolution.
3. Lok Sabha elects the members from both Houses through proportional representation by the single transferable vote; the term does not exceed one year
Wrong: each House elects its own members; Lok Sabha does not elect Rajya Sabha's.
4. Members are elected by the respective Houses through proportional representation by the single transferable vote; the term does not exceed one year
Correct: 20 members elected by Lok Sabha and 10 by Rajya Sabha through PR-STV, holding office for up to one year.

points: It considers the reports of the National Commissions for SCs and STs and examines welfare safeguards.

POL-R21-ORD-women-library-term.lead: Option 2: it is a joint committee of 30 (20 LS + 10 RS), constituted in 1997, that considers the reports of the National Commission for Women.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. It is a Lok Sabha committee of 15 members chaired by the Deputy Speaker
Wrong: a 15-member Lok Sabha committee chaired by the Deputy Speaker is the Private Members' Bills and Resolutions Committee; this committee is a joint committee of 30.
2. It is a joint committee of 30 members (20 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha), first constituted in 1997, which considers the reports of the National Commission for Women
Correct: it was constituted in 1997 and examines NCW reports and Union measures for women's status, dignity and equality.
3. It is a statutory body created by the National Commission for Women Act, 1990
Wrong: the NCW is a statutory body under the 1990 Act; this committee is a parliamentary committee that studies NCW reports.
4. It is a constitutional body set up under Article 15(3)
Wrong: Article 15(3) allows special provisions for women; it does not create this committee.

points: Note the year 1997, the same year Rajya Sabha set up its Ethics Committee.

POL-R21-PAC-CAG-autonomous-review.lead: Option 4: the CAG is not a member of the PAC, but assists it and is its 'friend, philosopher and guide'.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. The CAG is the ex officio Chairman of the Committee
Wrong: the PAC chairman is an MP appointed by the Speaker, not the CAG.
2. The CAG is a member of the Committee with the right to vote
Wrong: only MPs are members; the CAG has no vote.
3. The Committee directs the CAG's audit work and can recommend his removal
Wrong: the CAG is independent (Article 148) and can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge; the PAC cannot direct him.
4. The CAG is not a member, but assists the Committee in examining his audit reports and is called its 'friend, philosopher and guide'
Correct: the PAC examines the CAG's audit reports with the CAG's expert help.

points: CAG reports go to the President, who lays them before Parliament; then the PAC examines them.

POL-R21-PAC-appropriation-review.lead: Option 4: the PAC, assisted by the CAG, checks that money was spent on authorised purposes, in line with grants, with re-appropriations under the rules.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. The Estimates Committee itself conducts the statutory CAG audit and cancels the expenditure
Wrong: the CAG conducts audit; the Estimates Committee examines budget estimates and cannot cancel spending.
2. The Business Advisory Committee decides legality because it schedules financial business
Wrong: the Business Advisory Committee only allots time for House business; checking legality of spending is the PAC's work.
3. The PAC replaces the ministry and issues binding executive spending orders
Wrong: the PAC is not an executive body; it cannot issue orders or disallow expenditure.
4. The PAC, assisted by the CAG, checks authorised purposes, conformity with parliamentary grants and valid re-appropriation
Correct: these are exactly the PAC's checks on appropriation accounts.

points: Its work is a post-mortem of expenditure already incurred; recommendations are advisory.

POL-R21-PAC-chair-convention.lead: Option 1: the Speaker appoints the PAC chairman, and since 1967 the chairman has come from the Opposition by convention.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Lok Sabha Speaker; Opposition-chair convention since 1967
Correct: the chairman is appointed from members by the Speaker; until 1966–67 he was from the ruling party, after that from the Opposition.
2. President; Opposition-chair convention since 1950
Wrong: the President has no role, and the convention started in 1967, not 1950.
3. Rajya Sabha Chairman; Opposition-chair convention since 1921
Wrong: the Rajya Sabha Chairman does not appoint; 1921 is when the PAC was set up.
4. Finance Minister; chair must always be from the ruling party
Wrong: the Finance Minister has no role, and the chairman is not from the ruling party.

points: PAC: 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS), one-year term; ministers cannot be members.

POL-R21-PAC-policy-implementation-bounda.lead: Option 3: the PAC does not question broad policy, but can point out waste or extravagance in carrying it out.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. It substitutes its own broad policy for the approved policy, but cannot examine waste in implementation
Wrong: the PAC cannot replace Parliament's policy, and it can examine waste.
2. It must accept every implementing expenditure without comment once Parliament has approved the policy
Wrong: it does not accept every expenditure silently; examining waste is its main job.
3. It does not question broad policy, but may point out waste or extravagance and examine whether implementation was efficient and economical
Correct: Laxmikanth says it is not concerned with policy in the broad sense, yet examines expenditure for economy, prudence and propriety.
4. It may reconsider broad policy only after excluding all questions about the expenditure incurred under it
Wrong: it cannot reconsider broad policy at all, and it never excludes questions about expenditure.

points: Hook: policy = Parliament's choice; implementation = PAC's checking field.

POL-R21-PAC-retrospective-limits.lead: Option 2: the PAC reviews past expenditure and recommends corrective action; executive orders remain with the executive.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. It can retrospectively cancel the departmental expenditure and issue executive recovery orders itself.
Wrong: the PAC has no power to disallow expenditure or issue orders.
2. It reviews the past expenditure and recommends corrective action, while leaving day-to-day administration and executive orders to the executive.
Correct: its work is post-mortem and its recommendations are advisory.
3. It must approve every daily departmental payment before the expenditure occurs.
Wrong: it does not approve payments in advance and cannot interfere in day-to-day administration.
4. It must refuse to examine waste whenever the expenditure implements an approved policy.
Wrong: it does examine waste even under approved policy.

points: Only Parliament takes the final decision on its findings.

PRAC-POL-452548EE9DF7.lead: Both statements are correct, so option 3 ('Both 1 and 2').

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. PAC examines expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India.
True
It examines the appropriation accounts, which compare actual spending from the Consolidated Fund with what Parliament authorised in the Appropriation Act.
2. PAC also checks whether money was spent economically and wisely.
True
Laxmikanth says it examines spending not only for legality but also for economy, prudence, wisdom and propriety, to expose waste and extravagance.

points: Options 1 and 2 drop one true statement; option 4 rejects both.

LX-UPSC-2015-Q15.lead: Option 4: India has a parliamentary system because the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Article 75(3)).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Lok Sabha is directly elected
True fact, but direct election of the legislature exists in presidential systems too (the US House is directly elected). It does not define the system.
Parliament can amend the Constitution
True (Article 368), but amending power is about the Constitution, not about how the executive relates to the legislature.
Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved
True (it is a permanent House), but a permanent upper House exists in many systems and says nothing about executive responsibility.
Council of Ministers is responsible to Lok Sabha
The defining test: the executive survives only while it has the confidence of the popular House and can be removed by a no-confidence motion.

points: Parliamentary system = the executive is responsible to the legislature for its policies and acts; presidential system = executive is not responsible to the legislature.
Articles 74-75 (Centre) and 163-164 (States) set up this system.
