False
Its recommendations are not binding on the state government (LX p685).
2. Government must report action within one month
True
The government must inform it of action taken within one month (LX p685).
3. SHRC can punish a violator
False
It has no power to punish violators or to award relief itself (LX p685).

points: Option 1 includes false 1; option 3 includes false 3; option 4 includes both false statements.

POL-8.4.2-Q39.lead: Answer: option 2 (State Legislature). The SHRC's annual reports are laid before the state legislature with an action-taken memorandum.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Parliament
Receives NHRC reports, not SHRC reports.
2. State Legislature
The SHRC report is laid before each House of the state legislature.
3. Governor's Council
There is no 'Governor's Council' in the Act; SHRC reports go to the state government and are then laid before the state legislature.
4. NHRC
The SHRC submits its reports to the state government, not to the NHRC; the two commissions are independent.

points: LX p685: the SHRC submits reports to the state government; they are laid before the state legislature with a memorandum of action taken and reasons for not accepting any recommendation.

POL-8.4.2-Q40.lead: Answer: option 2 (Court of Session). The PHR Act, 1993 specifies a Court of Session in each district as the Human Rights Court for speedy trial.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Court of Judicial Magistrate
A lower criminal court; not the court named in the Act.
2. Court of Session
The district-level Sessions Court named as Human Rights Court.
3. Family Court
Deals with family and marriage disputes; not a Human Rights Court.
4. Lok Adalat
A forum for settling disputes by compromise; not a trial court for these offences.

points: LX p685: a Human Rights Court in every district for speedy trial, set up with the concurrence of the HC Chief Justice.
Section 30 of the Act specifies a Court of Session as the Human Rights Court.

POL-8.4.2-Q41.lead: Answer: option 1 (Chief Justice of the High Court). The state government specifies a Human Rights Court only with the concurrence of the HC Chief Justice.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Chief Justice of the High Court
Concurrence is required because the court is part of the state judiciary under the High Court.
2. Governor
The Act requires the concurrence of the High Court Chief Justice, not the Governor, for specifying a district Human Rights Court.
3. SHRC Chairperson
Has no role in setting up Human Rights Courts.
4. Chief Justice of India
The Chief Justice of India has no role here; district Human Rights Courts are specified with the concurrence of the state High Court's Chief Justice.

points: LX p685: 'These courts can be set up by the state government only with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court of that state.'

POL-8.4.2-Q42.lead: Answer: option 2 (7 years). The state government may appoint an advocate with at least seven years' practice as special public prosecutor.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. 5 years
Five years is not the figure; the Act requires an advocate who has practised for at least seven years.
2. 7 years
The prescribed practice for a special public prosecutor.
3. 10 years
Ten years is not the figure; seven years' practice is the requirement for a special public prosecutor.
4. 15 years
Fifteen years is not the figure; the Act asks for only seven years' practice as an advocate.

points: LX p685: for every Human Rights Court the state government specifies a public prosecutor or appoints an advocate who has practised for seven years as special public prosecutor.
Hook: 7 years again, like the District Judge member of the SHRC.

POL-8.4.2-Q43.lead: Option 2 (A-2, B-1, C-1, D-3) is correct. Appointer and salary differ; removal by the President is common.

head: List-I
Correct match (List-II)
Why / concept
rows: A. Appointed by the Governor
2. SHRC only
SHRC members are appointed by the Governor; NHRC members are appointed by the President, so it is SHRC only.
B. Salary fixed by the Centre
1. NHRC only
SHRC salary is fixed by the State government.
C. Seven ex-officio members
1. NHRC only
The NHRC has seven ex-officio members (heads of national commissions); an SHRC has no ex-officio members, so it is NHRC only.
D. Removed by the President
3. Both
Both are removed only by the President — even SHRC members, though the Governor appoints them.

points: Option 1 fails: it gives C-3 (Both NHRC and SHRC), D-2 (SHRC only); correct is C-1, D-3.
Option 3 fails: it gives A-1 (NHRC only), B-2 (SHRC only); correct is A-2, B-1.
Option 4 fails: it gives B-3 (Both NHRC and SHRC), D-1 (NHRC only); correct is B-1, D-3.

POL-8.4.2-Q44.lead: Option 1: an SHRC can inquire only into violations relating to subjects in the State List and the Concurrent List, while the NHRC has no such List limit.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: NHRC all Lists; SHRC only State and Concurrent Lists
Under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, an SHRC inquires only into violations on State List (List-II) and Concurrent List (List-III) subjects.
NHRC 5 years; SHRC 3 years
False. The 2019 Amendment cut the term of both NHRC and SHRC members from five to three years (or age 70).
NHRC constitutional; SHRC statutory
False. Both are statutory bodies created by the same 1993 Act; neither is named in the Constitution.
NHRC 3-year limit; SHRC 1-year limit
False. Both commissions cannot take up a matter after one year from the date of the alleged violation.

points: Tenure, legal status and limitation period are the same for both bodies; only the area of jurisdiction differs.
If a case is already before the NHRC or another statutory commission, the SHRC will not inquire into it.
Memory hook: State commission = State and Concurrent Lists.

POL-8.4.2-Q45.lead: Option 2: the 2019 Amendment says the Secretary of the SHRC exercises all its administrative and financial powers, subject to the Chairperson's control.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Chief Secretary of the state
The top civil servant of the state government; he is outside the Commission and has no role in running it.
Secretary of the SHRC, under the Chairperson
The Commission's own Secretary; the 2019 Amendment gave him all administrative and financial powers, subject to the Chairperson's control.
Senior-most member
A member does quasi-judicial work of inquiry; the Act gives no administrative control to the senior-most member.
Principal Secretary, Home
An officer of the state Home Department; giving him control would defeat the Commission's independence from government.

points: The same Amendment gave the NHRC's Secretary-General similar powers (except judicial functions and regulation-making), subject to the Chairperson.
The idea is to keep the Commission's day-to-day administration inside the Commission and away from the government it watches.

POL-8.4.2-Q46.lead: Option 2: Justice B. Subhashan Reddy was the first Chairperson of the combined Andhra Pradesh SHRC.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Justice K. Punnaiah
A former judge known for heading another state commission, not the first AP SHRC chairperson.
Justice B. Subhashan Reddy
Former Chief Justice of a High Court; he was the first Chairperson of the combined AP SHRC (set up in the mid-2000s) and later became AP Lokayukta.
Justice M. Seetharama Murti
He headed the AP SHRC after bifurcation, i.e. the residual Andhra Pradesh commission, not the first combined one.
Justice Shameem Akther
She is associated with the Telangana SHRC, a body created only after the 2014 bifurcation.

points: A State Human Rights Commission is created by the state government under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
The key word is 'combined': it points to the commission before the 2014 division of the state.

POL-8.4.2-Q47.lead: Option 1 (A-3, B-1, C-2) is correct. Current and recent human-rights commission chairs.

head: List-I
Correct match (List-II)
Why / concept
rows: A. Justice V. Ramasubramanian
3. NHRC Chairperson (2024)
Former SC judge, took over in December 2024.
B. Justice Shameem Akther
1. Telangana SHRC Chairperson (2025)
Justice Shameem Akther was appointed Telangana SHRC Chairperson in April 2025, so item 1 fits.
C. Justice M. Seetharama Murti
2. AP SHRC Chairperson (2021-2024)
Justice M. Seetharama Murti headed the AP SHRC from 2021; his term ended in 2024, so item 2 fits.

points: Option 2 fails: it gives A-1 (Telangana SHRC Chairperson (2025)), B-3 (NHRC Chairperson (2024)); correct is A-3, B-1.
Option 3 fails: it gives B-2 (AP SHRC Chairperson (2021-2024)), C-1 (Telangana SHRC Chairperson (2025)); correct is B-1, C-2.
Option 4 fails: it gives A-2 (AP SHRC Chairperson (2021-2024)), C-3 (NHRC Chairperson (2024)); correct is A-3, C-2.
Office-holders change; check the latest AP SHRC position before the exam.

POL-8.4.2-Q48.lead: Option 1: Justice Ranganath Misra, a former Chief Justice of India, was the first NHRC Chairperson (1993).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Justice Ranganath Misra
Former CJI; first Chairperson of the NHRC when it was set up in October 1993.
Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah
Former CJI; he was the second NHRC Chairperson, after Misra.
Justice J.S. Verma
Former CJI; he was the third NHRC Chairperson.
Justice A.S. Anand
Former CJI; he was the fourth NHRC Chairperson.

points: The NHRC was set up under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; it is statutory, not constitutional.
Until 2019 only a former CJI could be Chairperson; the 2019 Amendment also made a former Supreme Court judge eligible.
Memory hook: M-V-V-A = Misra, Venkatachaliah, Verma, Anand.

POL-8.4.2-Q49.lead: Option 2: the Governor appoints SHRC members, the state government fixes their salary, and only the President can remove them.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: President, Central government, Governor
Wrong on all three: the President does not appoint SHRC members, the Centre does not fix their salary, and the Governor cannot remove them.
Governor, State government, President
Correct: Governor appoints on a committee's advice (CM-led); salary is set by the state government; removal is only by the President.
Governor, Governor, Governor
Only the first is right; the Governor neither fixes salary by himself nor can remove members.
Governor, Central government, President
The salary part is wrong: for SHRC it is the state government; the Central government fixes salary only for NHRC.

points: Removal by the President, not the Governor, protects members from pressure by the state that appoints them.
For misbehaviour or incapacity, the President must first refer the matter to the Supreme Court.

POL-8.5.1-Q01.lead: Option 2: the Supreme Court has held that the right to know is part of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Article 14
Equality before law and equal protection of laws; not the source of RTI.
Article 19(1)(a)
Freedom of speech and expression; one cannot speak or express meaningfully without information, so the right to know is implied here.
Article 21A
Right to free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14.
Article 32
Right to constitutional remedies before the Supreme Court; it enforces rights, it is not the source of RTI.

points: The Constitution does not name RTI expressly; it is a judge-made inference.
The Court has also linked RTI with Article 21 (LX lists 'right to information' among Article 21 rights).

POL-8.5.1-Q02.lead: Option 2: in State of U.P. v. Raj Narain (1975) the Court said people have a right to know every public act done by public functionaries.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
1950 case on preventive detention and the meaning of 'procedure established by law' (Art 21).
State of U.P. v. Raj Narain
1975 case where the Court linked the right to know with Art 19(1)(a).
Bela Banerjee v. Union of India
1954 case on adequate compensation for acquisition of property.
Golaknath v. State of Punjab
1967 case holding Parliament could not amend Fundamental Rights.

points: Do not confuse it with Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975), the election case.
The 'right to know' idea from this case later grew into the RTI Act, 2005.

POL-8.5.1-Q03.lead: Option 4 (2, 4, 3, 1): Raj Narain judgment 1975, MKSS formed 1990, Tamil Nadu RTI law 1997, RTI Act in force 2005.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Puts Tamil Nadu (1997) before MKSS (1990), which is wrong.
Puts MKSS (1990) before the 1975 judgment, which is wrong.
Puts the 2005 Act before Tamil Nadu's 1997 law, which is wrong.

points: The judiciary recognised the idea first, a people's movement pushed it, states legislated, and then Parliament acted.
The RTI Act came fully into force on 12 October 2005.

POL-8.5.1-Q04.lead: Option 3: Sweden gave its people a legal right to information through the Freedom of the Press Act, 1766.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: USA
Passed its Freedom of Information Act in 1966, two centuries after Sweden.
Finland
Gained similar access rules early, but its modern law (1951) came long after Sweden.
Sweden
Freedom of the Press Act, 1766, the world's first legal right of access to official documents.
United Kingdom
Its Freedom of Information Act came only in 2000.

points: India's RTI Act (2005) is a late member of this global family.
Memory hook: Sweden 1766, the oldest.

POL-8.5.1-Q05.lead: Option 1: Aruna Roy co-founded the MKSS in Rajasthan, whose public hearings led the RTI movement.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Aruna Roy
Former IAS officer who co-founded the MKSS (1990) with Nikhil Dey and Shankar Singh; its jan sunwai on village records grew into the RTI movement.
Medha Patkar
Leader of the Narmada Bachao Andolan on dam displacement, not MKSS.
Kiran Bedi
India's first woman IPS officer, known for police and prison reform.
Ela Bhatt
Founder of SEWA, a union of self-employed women.

points: Jan sunwai means public hearing: villagers read out official records to expose false bills in public works.
This grassroots demand helped produce state RTI laws and then the RTI Act, 2005.

POL-8.5.1-Q06.lead: Option 3: Tamil Nadu and Goa both enacted RTI laws in 1997, before the national Act.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Maharashtra and Delhi
Delhi's law came in 2001 and Maharashtra's in 2002–03, not 1997.
Rajasthan and Karnataka
Rajasthan and Karnataka both enacted their RTI laws in 2000, three years after Tamil Nadu and Goa (1997).
Tamil Nadu and Goa
Both passed state RTI laws in 1997; Tamil Nadu was the first state.
Goa and Kerala
Goa is right, but Kerala was not among the 1997 states.

points: State laws showed that access to information could work, which helped push the national law.
Memory hook: 1997 = TN + Goa.

POL-8.5.1-Q07.lead: Only statement 1 is true, so the answer is option 1 (1 only).

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. RTI Act repealed FOI Act, 2002
True
Section 31 of the RTI Act repealed the Freedom of Information Act, 2002.
2. Fully in force on 15 June 2005
False
15 June 2005 is the date of Presidential assent; the Act came fully into force on 12 October 2005.

points: Option 2 is wrong because statement 2 confuses assent with full commencement.
Option 3 wrongly accepts statement 2; option 4 wrongly rejects the true statement 1.

POL-8.5.1-Q08.lead: Option 3: the RTI Act came fully into force on 12 October 2005.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 26 January 2005
Republic Day; no connection with the RTI Act.
15 June 2005
Date of Presidential assent, when only some sections began.
12 October 2005
The 120th day after assent, when the whole Act became operative.
1 November 2005
No RTI significance; often confused with state formation days.

points: Some sections (e.g. Sec 4(1), 5(1)-(2), 12, 13, 15, 16, 24) came into force at once on 15 June 2005, so offices could prepare.
12 October is observed as the RTI anniversary.

POL-8.5.1-Q09.lead: Option 2: Section 22 gives the RTI Act overriding effect over the Official Secrets Act, 1923 to the extent of any inconsistency.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: OSA prevails over RTI
False. Section 22 says the opposite: RTI prevails over inconsistent laws.
RTI prevails to the extent of inconsistency
True. Section 22 gives RTI an overriding effect; Section 8(2) also allows disclosure if public interest outweighs harm.
RTI repealed OSA
False. OSA 1923 is still in force; RTI repealed only the FOI Act, 2002.
RTI does not apply to documents marked 'secret'
False. A label does not decide; disclosure is decided by the Section 8 exemptions.

points: Overriding means both laws exist, but in a clash RTI wins.
Memory hook: Repeal = FOI 2002; Override = OSA 1923.

POL-8.5.1-Q10.lead: Answer: option 1 (both true, R explains A): Proactive disclosure serves the Act's goal of transparency.

head: Part
True/False
Why
rows: A
True
s.4(1)(b): every public authority must publish certain information suo motu.
R
True
The Act aims at transparency and accountability.

points: Does R explain A? Yes. The Act's object (R) is why s.4 requires disclosure even without a request (A).
Option 2 fails: R is not just a separate true fact; it is the very reason for A.
Options 3 and 4 fail: both A and R are true.

POL-8.5.1-Q11.lead: Option 3: information about a private body can be obtained through a public authority that can access it under any law in force (Section 2(f)).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: In no circumstances
False. Section 2(f) expressly includes private-body information that a public authority can access.
Directly from the private body with its own PIO
False. A purely private body is not a public authority and need not appoint a PIO.
Through a public authority that can access it under law
True. The request goes to the public authority (e.g. a regulator) that can obtain that information.
Only on a High Court order
False. No court order is needed; the normal RTI procedure applies.

points: Example: data a bank must file with a regulator can be sought from the regulator.
The private body is reached indirectly, never directly.

POL-8.5.1-Q12.lead: All three are included in Section 2(j), so the answer is option 4 (1, 2 and 3).

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. Inspection of works, documents, records
True
Section 2(j)(i) gives the right to inspect work, documents and records.
2. Taking certified samples of material
True
Section 2(j)(iii) allows taking certified samples of material.
3. Information in electronic form
True
Section 2(j)(iv) covers diskettes, floppies, tapes, video cassettes or other electronic modes.

points: Options 1, 2 and 3 each leave out one true item, so they are incomplete.
Section 2(j) also allows taking notes, extracts and certified copies.

POL-8.5.1-Q13.lead: Option 3: Section 3 says 'all citizens' shall have the right to information.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: All persons residing in India
Residence is not the test; the Act gives the right to citizens only.
Citizens and registered companies
A company is not a citizen, so it has no right under Section 3 in its own name.
All citizens
Section 3 says 'all citizens shall have the right to information', so the right belongs to citizens, matching this option exactly.
Only taxpayers
The Act sets no tax condition; every citizen, rich or poor, has the right.

points: Citizenship is the only qualification; no reason for asking is required (Sec 6(2)).
Persons below poverty line pay no application fee.

POL-8.5.1-Q14.lead: Option 1: putting such details online without any request is proactive disclosure under Section 4(1)(b).

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Section 4(1)(b) – proactive disclosure
Requires every public authority to publish its functions, officers' powers and duties, budget, PIO details and more on its own.
Section 6 – request
Applies only when a citizen asks; here nobody asked.
Section 8 – exemption
Lists what may be withheld; the corporation is disclosing, not withholding.
Section 19 – appeal
Remedy against a PIO's decision; no dispute exists here.

points: The key words are 'without anyone asking' – that is suo motu disclosure.
Good suo motu disclosure reduces the number of RTI applications.

POL-8.5.1-Q15.lead: Statements 2 and 3 are true and 1 is false, so the answer is option 2.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. Applicant must state reason
False
Section 6(2) says the applicant need not give any reason for seeking information.
2. Only contact details needed
True
Section 6(2) says no personal details are required except those needed to contact the applicant.
3. English, Hindi or official language of the area
True
Section 6(1) allows the request in English, Hindi or the official language of the area.

points: Options 1, 3 and 4 all include the false statement 1.

Option 2 fails: R is not just a separate true fact; it is the very reason for A.
Options 3 and 4 fail: both A and R are true.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. Lokpal Bills were introduced between 1968 and 2001, but none became law
True
Bills of 1968, 1971, 1977, 1985, 1996, 1998 and 2001 lapsed on dissolution of the Lok Sabha, and the 1989 Bill was withdrawn, so none became law.
2. The 2011 Bill was passed in 2013 and got assent on 1 January 2014
True
The tenth Bill (December 2011) was passed by Parliament in December 2013 and received assent on 1 January 2014, becoming the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.

points: Options 1 and 2 each reject one true statement, and option 4 rejects both.
Of the two 2011 Bills, the August 2011 Bill was withdrawn; the December 2011 Bill became law.

POL-8.6.1-Q14.lead: Option 4: Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose was not a drafter of the Jan Lokpal Bill; he became the first Chairperson of the Lokpal in 2019.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Anna Hazare
Anna Hazare led the 2011 civil-society movement that pushed the Jan Lokpal draft.
Santosh Hegde
Former Karnataka Lokayukta Santosh Hegde was one of the civil-society members who drafted it.
Arvind Kejriwal
Arvind Kejriwal was a key civil-society drafter of the Jan Lokpal Bill.
Pinaki Chandra Ghose
He was a Supreme Court judge and later the first Lokpal Chairperson; he had no role in the civil-society draft.

points: The question uses NOT, so we look for the person outside the 2011 movement.
The government's own Bill (December 2011), not the Jan Lokpal draft, became the 2013 Act.

POL-8.6.1-Q15.lead: Option 1 (2, 1, 3, 4): tenth Bill (December 2011), assent (1 January 2014), commencement (16 January 2014), first Chairperson (March 2019).

head: Event
Date
Why it comes here
rows: 2. Introduction of the tenth Lokpal Bill
December 2011
A Bill must be introduced before it can be passed or signed.
1. President's assent
1 January 2014
After Parliament passed it in December 2013, the President signed it.
3. Commencement of the Act
16 January 2014
An Act comes into force only after assent, here about two weeks later.
4. Appointment of the first Chairperson
March 2019
Justice P.C. Ghose was appointed only in 2019, five years after the Act came into force.

points: Option 2 starts with assent, but a Bill cannot be signed before it is introduced.
Option 3 puts commencement before assent, which is legally impossible.
Option 4 puts the Chairperson before commencement, but no one can be appointed under an Act not yet in force.

POL-8.6.1-Q16.lead: Option 3: the Lokpal is a statutory body, created by an Act of Parliament, the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Constitutional body
A constitutional body is created by an Article of the Constitution (e.g. Election Commission, Art. 324). No Article provides for the Lokpal.
Executive body created by resolution
An executive body is set up by a government order or resolution (as the CVC was in 1964). The Lokpal was set up by law, not by resolution.
Statutory body
A statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament; the Lokpal comes from the 2013 Act.
Non-statutory advisory body
It is neither non-statutory nor merely advisory; it can inquire, investigate and order prosecution.

points: Test: ask 'what created it?' Constitution = constitutional; Act = statutory; government order = executive.
Compare: CVC began as an executive body (1964) and became statutory in 2003.

POL-8.6.1-Q17.lead: Option 4 (1 and 2 only): the Lokpal has a Chairperson and up to eight members, half of them judicial; the 50 per cent social quota is a combined one, not for women alone.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. Chairperson and a maximum of eight members
True
The Act provides for a Chairperson and not more than eight members.
2. Half of the members must be judicial members
True
50 per cent of the members must be judicial members.
3. Half of the members must be women
False
The 50 per cent quota is for SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women together; women are one of five groups, not a separate 50 per cent.

points: Options 2 and 3 include false statement 3.
Option 1 leaves out true statement 2.
The judicial and social quotas can overlap: a judicial member can also be from an SC/ST/OBC/minority group or a woman.

POL-8.6.1-Q18.lead: Option 3: 50 per cent of 8 members is 4.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Two is only 25 per cent of eight members; the Act requires 50 per cent.
Three is less than half of eight, so it falls short of the quota.
Half of eight members is four, which meets the 50 per cent requirement for SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women.
Five is more than half; the law sets a minimum of 50 per cent, and four already meets it.

points: The quota counts members, not the Chairperson.
These four can also be judicial members, as the two quotas overlap.

POL-8.6.1-Q19.lead: Option 4: a sitting High Court Chief Justice is eligible only as a judicial member of the Lokpal, not as its Chairperson.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: A former Chief Justice of India
Eligible: a person who is or has been CJI can be Chairperson.
A former judge of the Supreme Court
Eligible: a person who is or has been an SC judge can be Chairperson.
An eminent person with 25 years' expertise in vigilance
Eligible: an eminent person with at least 25 years' expertise in fields like anti-corruption policy, vigilance, public administration, finance, law or management can be Chairperson.
A sitting Chief Justice of a High Court
Not eligible as Chairperson: a High Court Chief Justice qualifies only to be a judicial member.

points: The question asks for the person NOT eligible.
Hook: Chairperson needs CJI or SC-judge level (or 25-year eminent person); HC Chief Justice level is for judicial members.

POL-8.6.1-Q20.lead: Option 1: a judicial member must be (or have been) a Supreme Court judge or a High Court Chief Justice.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: A former SC judge or former HC Chief Justice
Correct: this is the qualification the Act lays down for a judicial member.
A former HC judge with 10 years' service
An ordinary HC judge, however long-serving, does not qualify; it must be a Chief Justice of a High Court.
An advocate with 20 years' practice
Advocates are not eligible as judicial members; they could only qualify as an eminent non-judicial member if they meet the 25-year test.
A former District Judge
District judges are too junior; the minimum is HC Chief Justice level.

points: The Act's words are 'is or has been', so a sitting SC judge or HC Chief Justice also qualifies; among the options, option 1 is the only correct one.
Half of the Lokpal's members must be judicial members.

POL-8.6.1-Q21.lead: Option 3: the Rajya Sabha Chairman is not a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Speaker of Lok Sabha
Member: the Speaker sits on the Selection Committee.
Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha
Member: the LoP in the Lok Sabha is on the committee.
Chairman of Rajya Sabha
Not a member: the 2013 Act does not include him. He appeared only in the First ARC's 1966 consultation idea.
An eminent jurist
Member: the President nominates an eminent jurist on the recommendation of the other four members.

points: The five members: PM (chair), Lok Sabha Speaker, LoP in Lok Sabha, CJI or an SC judge nominated by him, and an eminent jurist.
Trap: the ARC's list (CJI, Speaker, RS Chairman) and the 2013 Act's list are different.

POL-8.6.1-Q22.lead: Option 3 (1 and 2 only): the PM chairs the committee and the CJI may send an SC judge, but the eminent jurist is nominated by the President, not the CJI.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. It is chaired by the Prime Minister
True
The Prime Minister chairs the Lokpal Selection Committee.
2. The CJI may nominate a Supreme Court judge in his place
True
The member is the CJI or a sitting SC judge nominated by the CJI.
3. The eminent jurist is nominated by the CJI
False
The President nominates the eminent jurist on the recommendation of the first four members of the committee.

points: Options 2 and 4 include false statement 3.
Option 1 leaves out true statement 2.

POL-8.6.1-Q23.lead: Answer: option 2 (both true, R does not explain A): Both are features of s.4, but the purpose of the Search Committee does not explain its diversity rule.

head: Part
True/False
Why
rows: A
True
At least 50% of Search Committee members must be from SC/ST/OBC/minorities/women.
R
True
The Search Committee prepares a panel for the Selection Committee.

points: Does R explain A? No. R tells what the committee does; A tells who must sit on it. The diversity rule is a separate social-justice safeguard.
Option 1 fails: R is true, but it does not give the reason for A.
Options 3 and 4 fail: both statements are true.

POL-8.6.1-Q24.lead: Option 3: the Chairperson addresses the resignation to the President, who appoints him.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Prime Minister
The PM only chairs the Selection Committee; he is not the appointing authority.
Chief Justice of India
The CJI is a member of the Selection Committee only; he does not receive the resignation.
President
The President appoints the Chairperson by warrant under his hand and seal, so the resignation goes to him.
Speaker of Lok Sabha
The Speaker is a Selection Committee member only.

points: General rule: resignation is addressed to the appointing authority.
Removal is also by the President, after a Supreme Court inquiry.

POL-8.6.1-Q25.lead: Option 4 (1, 2 and 3): all three persons are disqualified.

head: Person
Disqualified?
Why
rows: 1. A sitting member of a Municipal Corporation
Yes
The Act bars members of a Panchayat or Municipality, just as it bars MPs and MLAs, to keep the Lokpal non-political.
2. A person aged 44 years
Yes
A person must be at least 45 years old on the date of assuming office.
3. A person dismissed from government service
Yes
A person removed or dismissed from the service of the Union or a State is not eligible.

points: Options 1, 2 and 3 each leave out one disqualified person, so they fail.
Other bars: conviction for moral turpitude, office of profit, link with a political party, or carrying on business or a profession.

POL-8.6.1-Q26.lead: Option 1: he can serve 3 more years, because total service as Member and Chairperson cannot exceed 5 years, and he reaches only 69 by then.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 3 years
5 years total minus the 2 years already served as member = 3 years; at 69 he is still below the age limit of 70.
4 years
Four more years would make his total 6 years, above the 5-year cap.
5 years
A fresh 5 years would ignore the 2 years already served; the cap is on total tenure.
Until age 75
The age limit is 70, not 75, and the 5-year total cap would end it earlier anyway.

points: Rule: term is 5 years or until age 70, whichever is earlier.
Step: 66 + 3 = 69, which is below 70, so the 5-year total cap decides.

POL-8.6.1-Q27.lead: Option 2 (1 and 2 only): reappointment and posts like diplomat or UT administrator are barred, but the election bar lasts only five years, not for life.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. Ineligible for reappointment as Chairperson or Member
True
After ceasing to hold office he cannot be reappointed to the Lokpal at all.
2. Cannot get a diplomatic assignment or be made UT administrator
True
The Act bars diplomatic assignments, appointment as administrator of a UT and other such government posts.
3. Barred for life from contesting election to Parliament
False
The bar on contesting elections (President, Vice-President, Parliament, State Legislature, local bodies) lasts only five years after leaving office.

points: Options 3 and 4 include false statement 3 (the word 'for life').
Option 1 leaves out true statement 2.
The aim is to stop the Chairperson from pleasing the government in the hope of a post-retirement reward.

POL-8.6.1-Q28.lead: Answer: option 2 (both true, R does not explain A): Both are removal rules, but R does not explain A.

head: Part
True/False
Why
rows: A
True
For misbehaviour, the President removes only after an SC inquiry (on reference, e.g. petition of 100+ MPs).
R
True
True. Under the Lokpal Act, the President can remove the Chairperson or a member directly, without any SC inquiry, if he is adjudged insolvent.

points: Does R explain A? No. R gives a separate direct ground of removal; it does not explain why misbehaviour needs an SC inquiry.
Option 1 fails: R is true, but it does not give the reason for A.
Options 3 and 4 fail: both statements are true.

POL-8.6.1-Q29.lead: Option 1 (a-2, b-1) is correct. Lokpal salaries.

head: List-I
Correct match (List-II)
Why / concept
rows: a. Chairperson
2. Chief Justice of India
The Lokpal Chairperson's salary and conditions are the same as the Chief Justice of India — top judicial parity.
b. Members
1. Judge of the Supreme Court
Same salary and conditions as a Supreme Court judge.

points: Option 2 fails: it gives A-1 (Judge of the Supreme Court), B-2 (Chief Justice of India); correct is A-2, B-1.
Option 3 fails: it gives B-3 (Chief Justice of a High Court); correct is B-1.
Option 4 fails: it gives A-3 (Chief Justice of a High Court); correct is A-2.
HC Chief Justice parity (3) is for some State Lokayuktas, not Lokpal.

POL-8.6.1-Q30.lead: Option 4: the Lokpal submits its annual report to the President, who has it laid before both Houses of Parliament.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Prime Minister
The PM chairs the Selection Committee but does not receive the report; the Lokpal can inquire into the PM himself.
Central Vigilance Commissioner
The CVC works under the Lokpal's reference in some cases; it is not the authority the Lokpal reports to.
Speaker of Lok Sabha
The report reaches Parliament through the President, not directly through the Speaker.
President
The President receives the report and causes it to be laid before each House.

points: State Lokayuktas report to the Governor, who lays the report before the state legislature.
Hook: appointed by the President, reports to the President.

POL-8.6.1-Q31.lead: Option 1: the complaint is barred because the Lokpal cannot take up complaints filed more than 7 years after the alleged offence; 2017 to 2026 is about 9 years.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Complaint is barred as it is beyond 7 years
The Act sets a limitation period of 7 years from the date of the alleged offence, and this complaint is about 9 years late.
Lokpal will inquire as there is no time limit
Wrong: there is a 7-year limit, which critics list as a drawback.
Lokpal must refer it to the CBI
Reference to an agency happens only for complaints the Lokpal can take up; a time-barred complaint is not taken up at all.
Complaint can be taken only with the President's permission
The Act gives no such President's permission route for time-barred complaints.

points: Limitation period means the time window within which a complaint must be filed.
Critics say 7 years is too short for big corruption that comes to light late.

POL-8.6.1-Q32.lead: Option 4: officers of a State Government are outside the Lokpal; they fall under that state's Lokayukta.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Union Ministers
Covered: the Lokpal's jurisdiction includes Union Ministers.
Members of Parliament
Covered: MPs are within the Lokpal's jurisdiction.
Group D employees of the Central Government
Covered: all Groups A, B, C and D of the Central Government are included (C and D through the CVC).
Officers of a State Government
Not covered: the Lokpal is a Union body; state officials are dealt with by the state Lokayukta.

points: Simple rule: Centre = Lokpal; State = Lokayukta.
The PM is also covered, with special safeguards.

POL-8.6.1-Q33.lead: Option 2 (1, 2 and 3 only): international relations, public order, and atomic energy and space are excluded; disinvestment is not.

head: Subject
Excluded?
Why
rows: 1. International relations
Yes
The Act excludes allegations against the PM relating to international relations, as these are sensitive foreign policy matters.
2. Public order
Yes
Public order is one of the listed excluded subjects.
3. Atomic energy and space
Yes
Atomic energy and space are excluded for reasons of national security and secrecy.
4. Disinvestment of PSUs
No
Disinvestment is an economic decision and is not on the excluded list, so the Lokpal can inquire into it.

points: Option 1 wrongly leaves out public order.
Options 3 and 4 wrongly include disinvestment.
The other excluded area is external and internal security.

POL-8.6.1-Q34.lead: Option 1 (1 and 2 only): an inquiry against the PM needs two-thirds of the Full Bench and is held in camera; if dismissed, the records are not published.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. Requires approval of at least two-thirds of the Full Bench
True
The Full Bench (Chairperson and all members) must consider it, and at least two-thirds must approve the inquiry.
2. It must be held in camera
True
The inquiry is held in camera (in private), to protect the office of the PM.
3. If the complaint is dismissed, the records are published
False
If the complaint is dismissed, the records are not published or made available to anyone.

points: Options 3 and 4 include false statement 3.
Option 2 leaves out true statement 2.
This secrecy is why critics call the PM procedure 'very non-transparent'.

POL-8.6.1-Q35.lead: Option 2: the Lokpal has its own Inquiry Wing and Prosecution Wing.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Vigilance Wing and Audit Wing
Audit of government accounts is the CAG's job; the Lokpal has no audit wing.
Inquiry Wing and Prosecution Wing
The Act gives the Lokpal an Inquiry Wing for preliminary inquiries and a Prosecution Wing to prosecute public servants.
Intelligence Wing and Police Wing
The Lokpal has no police or intelligence wing; it uses agencies like the CBI for investigation.
Legal Wing and Finance Wing
These are not the two wings named by the Act.

points: The Inquiry Wing is headed by a Director of Inquiry and the Prosecution Wing by a Director of Prosecution.
Hook: Lokpal inquires and prosecutes; courts punish.

POL-8.6.1-Q36.lead: Answer: option 3 (A true, R false): The CBI Director is chosen by a PM-led committee, not the Lokpal.

head: Part
True/False
Why
rows: A
True
Lokpal has superintendence and direction over CBI for cases referred by it.
R
False
False: the CBI Director is recommended by a committee of PM, LoP/single largest opposition leader and CJI.

points: Does R explain A? No link: R is false.
Options 1 and 2 fail: they treat R as true, but R is false.
Option 4 fails: A is a correct statement.

POL-8.6.1-Q37.lead: Option 1: for Group C and D employees, the CVC proceeds under its own powers, subject to reporting to and review by the Lokpal.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: CVC proceeds under its own powers, subject to Lokpal review
For Groups C and D, the CVC acts itself under the CVC Act, and the Lokpal reviews its work.
CVC sends findings back to Lokpal for decision
This is the procedure for Group A and B officers, not Group C.
CVC must forward it to the CBI
There is no compulsory CBI routing in this procedure.
Ministry decides without CVC
Wrong: the Lokpal referred it to the CVC, so the CVC must act; the ministry cannot bypass it.

points: Hook: senior officers (A, B) - the Lokpal decides; junior staff (C, D) - the CVC decides, the Lokpal watches.

POL-8.6.1-Q38.lead: Option 2 (1 and 3 only): a society partly financed by the government and an NGO getting foreign money above Rs 10 lakh a year are covered; a merely aided body is not.

head: Entity
Covered?
Why
rows: 1. A society financed partly by the government
Yes
Institutions financed fully or partly by the government are within Lokpal jurisdiction.
2. A body merely aided by the government
No
The Act expressly excludes institutions that are only aided by the government.
3. An NGO receiving foreign contribution of Rs 15 lakh a year
Yes
Entities receiving foreign donations under FCRA above Rs 10 lakh a year are covered, and Rs 15 lakh is above that.

points: Option 1 leaves out the FCRA NGO.
Options 3 and 4 wrongly include the merely aided body.
'Financed' means the government funds it; 'aided' means only occasional support.

POL-8.6.1-Q39.lead: Option 4 (1, 2 and 3): all three are CBI-strengthening provisions of the 2013 Act.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. Directorate of Prosecution under the overall control of the CBI Director
True
The Act set up a Directorate of Prosecution, headed by a Director, under the overall supervision and control of the CBI Director.
2. Director of Prosecution appointed on CVC's recommendation
True
The Central Government appoints the Director of Prosecution on the recommendation of the CVC.
3. Transfer of CBI officers on Lokpal cases only with Lokpal approval
True
Officers investigating Lokpal-referred cases can be transferred only with the Lokpal's approval, to stop interference.

points: Options 1, 2 and 3 each leave out one true statement.
Other provisions: a panel of non-government advocates with Lokpal consent, and adequate funds for Lokpal-referred cases.

POL-8.6.1-Q40.lead: Option 2 (a-2, b-3, c-1) is correct. Lokpal Act time limits.

head: List-I
Correct match (List-II)
Why / concept
rows: a. Preliminary enquiry
2. 3 months + 3 months
Quick check whether a prima facie case exists.
b. Investigation
3. 6 months + 6 months at a time
Full investigation by the Lokpal's wing or an agency.
c. Trial
1. 1 year + 1 year
The trial in special courts should be completed within 1 year, extendable by 1 year, so item 1 fits.

points: Option 1 fails: it gives A-3 (6 months, extendable by 6 months at a time), B-2 (3 months, extendable by 3 months); correct is A-2, B-3.
Option 3 fails: it gives B-1 (1 year, extendable by 1 year), C-3 (6 months, extendable by 6 months at a time); correct is B-3, C-1.
Option 4 fails: it gives A-1 (1 year, extendable by 1 year), C-2 (3 months, extendable by 3 months); correct is A-2, C-1.
Hook: 3 → 6 → 12 months, each doubling.

POL-8.6.1-Q41.lead: Option 1: the 2013 Act raised the maximum punishment under the Prevention of Corruption Act from 7 to 10 years.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 7 to 10 years
Correct: the maximum went up from seven years to ten years.
5 to 7 years
Seven was the old maximum, not the new one.
7 to 14 years
Fourteen years is not the new maximum; it is ten.
10 years to life
The Act did not make corruption punishable with life imprisonment.

points: The minimum punishment under sections 7, 8, 9 and 12 of the PC Act became three years.
The minimum for attempt (section 15) became two years.

POL-8.6.1-Q42.lead: Option 2 (1 and 2 only): the Lokpal can grant sanction and attach property, but it cannot itself sentence anyone to prison.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. It can grant sanction for prosecution
True
The Act gave the power to grant sanction for prosecution to the Lokpal, in place of the government or competent authority.
2. It can attach corruptly acquired property while prosecution is pending
True
The Act allows attachment and confiscation of such property even while the case is still going on.
3. It can award imprisonment itself
False
Punishment is given only by a court (special courts for these trials). The Lokpal inquires and prosecutes but does not convict.

points: Options 3 and 4 include false statement 3.
Option 1 leaves out true statement 2.

POL-8.6.1-Q43.lead: Option 4: 'Lokpal has no power over the CBI' is NOT a criticism, because it is false: the Lokpal can supervise and direct the CBI in cases it refers.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Lokpal cannot act suo motu
A real criticism: the Lokpal cannot proceed against a public servant on its own initiative.
Anonymous complaints are not allowed
A real criticism: complaints must be in the prescribed form; anonymous ones are not accepted.
Accused public servant gets legal assistance
A real criticism: the Act gives legal help to the public servant accused, which critics see as unfair.
Lokpal has no power over the CBI
Not a criticism, because the Act actually gives the Lokpal superintendence and direction over the CBI for cases it refers.

points: The question asks for the statement that is NOT a criticism.
Other drawbacks: emphasis on form over substance, heavy penalty for false complaints, 7-year limit and a non-transparent PM procedure.

POL-8.6.1-Q44.lead: Answer: option 2 (both true, R does not explain A): Both are listed drawbacks; R does not cause A.

head: Part
True/False
Why
rows: A
True
Heavy punishment for false complaints may deter complainants.
R
True
True. The Lokpal can act only on a complaint; it has no power to start an inquiry suo motu on its own.

points: Does R explain A? No. A is about fear of penalty; R is about who can start a case. Two separate drawbacks.
Option 1 fails: R is true, but it does not give the reason for A.
Options 3 and 4 fail: both statements are true.

POL-8.6.1-Q45.lead: Option 2: states had to set up Lokayuktas by a state law within 365 days of the Act's commencement.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 180 days
Six months is not the period given in the Act.
365 days
Section 63 requires each state to set up a Lokayukta by law within 365 days.
2 years
Two years is not the period in the Act; Section 63 gives states 365 days (one year) to set up Lokayuktas.
No time limit
Wrong: the Act made it mandatory and gave a fixed deadline.

points: States are free to decide the design of their Lokayukta; only setting one up is compulsory.
Counting starts from commencement (16 January 2014).

POL-8.6.1-Q46.lead: Option 3: both are correct. Odisha passed a Lokayukta Act first (1970), and Maharashtra set up the institution first (1971).

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. Odisha passed a Lokayukta Act in 1970
True
Odisha legislated first, in 1970, but its institution started working later.
2. Maharashtra was first to establish the Lokayukta, in 1971
True
Maharashtra was the first state where the Lokayukta was actually established, in 1971.

points: Options 1 and 2 each reject one true statement; option 4 rejects both.
Both statements fit together: one is about passing the law, the other about setting up the body.

POL-8.6.1-Q47.lead: Option 2: in most states the Lokayukta serves 5 years or until age 65, whichever is earlier; at 63 he reaches 65 in 2 years.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: After 5 years
He would be 68 after 5 years, but the age limit of 65 comes first.
On reaching 65
At 63, he reaches 65 after 2 years, earlier than the 5-year term, so this ends his term.
On reaching 70
Age 70 is the limit for the central Lokpal, not the usual state Lokayukta.
At the Governor's pleasure
The Lokayukta has a fixed term for independence; he does not hold office at the Governor's pleasure.

points: 'Whichever is earlier' means you work out both dates and pick the first.
The Governor appoints the Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta.

POL-8.6.1-Q48.lead: Option 2 (2 and 3 only): Lokayukta recommendations are advisory and the Governor lays its report before the legislature, but CM coverage is not uniform.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. The Chief Minister is covered uniformly in all states
False
The CM is included in some states and excluded in others; there is no uniformity.
2. Their recommendations are advisory and not binding
True
The Lokayukta's recommendations are only advisory and not binding on the state government.
3. The annual report is laid before the legislature by the Governor
True
The Lokayukta reports annually to the Governor, who places it with an explanatory memorandum before the state legislature.

points: Options 1, 3 and 4 include false statement 1.
The lack of binding power is a key weakness of state Lokayuktas.

POL-8.6.1-Q49.lead: Option 4 (1, 2 and 3): all three are features of the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta under the AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983.

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. No complaints on events older than six years
True
A complaint made more than six years after the action complained of can be rejected under the AP Act.
2. It may inquire on a reference by the Governor
True
Under the AP Act the Lokayukta is not limited to citizens' complaints; a matter can also reach it on a reference by the Governor.
3. Department must report action within three months
True
Under Section 12(2), the competent authority must tell the Lokayukta within three months what action it has taken or proposes on its report.

points: Option 2 and Option 3 include false statement 2; Option 4 rejects true statement 1.

POL-8.6.2-Q47.lead: Option 1. The Governor does NOT chair the selection committee; the Chief Minister heads it.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Chairing the selection committee
The selection committee is headed by the Chief Minister, not the Governor, so this is the role he does NOT perform.
Removing after legislature's address
The Governor removes the Lokayukta after each House passes an address by special majority.
Appointing the Lokayukta
The Governor appoints the Lokayukta by warrant under his hand and seal (LX p727).
Placing annual report before legislature
The Governor places the annual report with an explanatory memorandum before the legislature (LX p728).

points: The Governor is the formal head: appoints, removes, receives reports and tables them.
The committee recommends; the Governor acts on it.

POL-9.1.1-Q01.lead: Morarji Desai. He was the first chairman of the First ARC (1966); K. Hanumanthayya took over when Desai joined the Union Cabinet.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Morarji Desai
Chaired the six-member First ARC when it was set up in 1966 (LX p237).
K. Hanumanthayya
Became chairman later, after Morarji Desai left (LX p237).
Veerappa Moily
Chaired the Second ARC set up in 2005, not the first.
M.C. Setalvad
Headed only the ARC's study team on Centre-State relations (LX p237).

points: Laxmikanth: the Central government appointed a six-member First ARC in 1966 under Morarji Desai (followed by K. Hanumanthayya) (LX p237).
The same ARC, under Desai, recommended the Lokpal and Lokayukta in 1966 (LX p723).
POL-9.1.1-Q01.also: Its Centre-State report (1969, 22 recommendations) built on the study team headed by M.C. Setalvad (LX p237).

POL-9.1.1-Q02.lead: M.C. Setalvad. The First ARC set up a study team under him to examine Centre-State relations.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: K. Santhanam
Headed the Committee on Prevention of Corruption (1962-64), which led to the CVC.
M.C. Setalvad
India's first Attorney-General; headed the ARC study team on Centre-State relations (LX p237).
R.S. Sarkaria
Retired SC judge who headed the Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations (1983-88) (LX p238).
P.V. Rajamannar
Headed the committee appointed by Tamil Nadu in 1969 (LX p237).

points: On the basis of the Setalvad study team's report, the ARC finalised its own report and submitted it in 1969 (LX p237).
Hook: ARC → Setalvad study team; Tamil Nadu → Rajamannar; Centre 1983 → Sarkaria.

POL-9.1.1-Q03.lead: Statements 1 and 2 are true and 3 is false, so the answer is Option 1 (1 and 2 only).

True/False
Why

True
The ARC submitted its report in 1969 and made 22 recommendations on Centre-State relations (LX p237).
2. Recommended an Inter-State Council under Article 263
True
Establishing an Inter-State Council under Article 263 was the first of its important recommendations (LX p237).
3. Most recommendations implemented immediately
False
Laxmikanth says no action was taken by the Central government on the ARC's recommendations (LX p237).

points: Option 2 (2 and 3), Option 3 (1 and 3) and Option 4 (1, 2 and 3) all include false statement 3.
The Inter-State Council was finally set up only in 1990, after the Sarkaria Commission also recommended it.

POL-9.1.1-Q04.lead: Answer: option 4 (A false, R true): The First ARC allowed deployment "on request or otherwise".

True/False
Why

False
False: the First ARC said Central forces may be deployed either on the State's request or otherwise.
R
True
Sarkaria: the Centre may deploy forces even without State consent, though it should consult the State.

points: Does R explain A? No link: A is false.
Options 1, 2 and 3 fail: each of them treats A as true, but A is false.

POL-9.1.1-Q05.lead: The Government of Tamil Nadu. The DMK government appointed the Rajamannar Committee in 1969 to seek maximum autonomy for states.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: The Union Government
The Centre appointed the ARC (1966) and Sarkaria Commission (1983), not Rajamannar.
The Government of Kerala
The Government of Kerala did not appoint this committee; it was appointed by the DMK government of Tamil Nadu in 1969.
The Government of West Bengal
Its contribution was the 1977 Memorandum on Centre-State relations, not a committee (LX p238).
The Government of Tamil Nadu
Appointed the three-member committee under Dr P.V. Rajamannar in 1969 (LX p237).

points: The committee reported to the Tamil Nadu Government in 1971; the Central government completely ignored it (LX p237-238).
It blamed unitary trends on special Central powers, one-party rule, weak state finances and Central planning (LX p237-238).

POL-9.1.1-Q06.lead: Option 4. Rajamannar wanted residuary powers allocated to the states, not kept with Parliament.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: A permanent Finance Commission
Was a Rajamannar recommendation — make the Finance Commission permanent (LX p238).
Abolition of the Planning Commission
Was a recommendation — disband it and replace it with a statutory body (LX p238).
Omission of Articles 356, 357 and 365
Was a recommendation — totally omit the President's Rule provisions (LX p238).
Residuary powers to remain with Parliament
NOT a recommendation; it said residuary powers should go to the states (LX p238).

points: Other Rajamannar demands: Inter-State Council immediately, shift some Union/Concurrent subjects to the State List, abolish All-India Services (LX p238).
In a 'NOT' question, pick the option that contradicts the body's stand.

POL-9.1.1-Q07.lead: Communications. The Anandpur Sahib Resolution wanted the Centre limited to defence, foreign affairs, communications and currency.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?

Communications
One of the four subjects the Akali Dal wanted to leave with the Centre (LX p238).
Inter-state trade
Inter-state trade was not one of the four subjects (defence, foreign affairs, currency, communications) the resolution left with the Centre.

points: Adopted by the Akali Dal in 1973 at Anandpur Sahib, Punjab; it also wanted all residuary powers vested in the states (LX p238).
Hook: 'DFCC' — Defence, Foreign affairs, Communications, Currency.

3. Repeal Articles 356, 357 and 360
True
It wanted Articles 356 and 357 (President's Rule) and 360 (financial emergency) repealed (LX p238).

points: Options 1, 2 and 3 each leave out one true demand.

The Centre appointed the Sarkaria Commission under Justice R.S. Sarkaria in 1983 to review all Centre-State arrangements.

True

points: Option 1 and option 2 each leave out one true statement.

POL-9.1.1-Q12.lead: Option 4: the Sarkaria Commission said over-centralisation leads to 'blood pressure at the centre and anaemia at the periphery'.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Punchhi Commission
Second Centre-State commission (2007-2010); its keynote was 'cooperative federalism', not this phrase.
Rajamannar Committee
Tamil Nadu's 1969 committee that wanted utmost autonomy for states; it did not coin this phrase.
Second ARC
Administrative Reforms Commission of 2005 under Veerappa Moily; it dealt with administration, not this phrase.
Sarkaria Commission
It wanted a strong Centre but warned that a strong Centre is not the same as centralisation; too much centralisation makes the Centre 'sick' and states 'weak'.

points: Meaning: power piled up at the Centre (high blood pressure) while states lack strength (anaemia) - both are unhealthy (LX p239).
Sarkaria saw federalism as a functional arrangement for co-operative action, not a static concept (LX p238).

POL-9.1.1-Q13.lead: Answer: option 1 (both true, R explains A): Its co-operative view of federalism explains why it avoided structural change.

head: Part
True/False
Why
rows: A
True
Sarkaria did not favour structural changes.
R
True
It saw federalism as a functional arrangement for co-operative action.

points: Does R explain A? Yes. If federalism is about working together (R), you improve working, not structure (A).
Option 2 fails: R is not just a separate true fact; it is the very reason for A.
Options 3 and 4 fail: both A and R are true.

POL-9.1.1-Q14.lead: Option 3: Sarkaria said the Centre should consult the states before making a law on a Concurrent List subject.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Abolish the Concurrent List
Sarkaria did not favour structural changes; it kept the three-list scheme as basically sound.
Two-thirds Rajya Sabha majority
This resembles Article 249 (Parliament legislating on a State List subject); Sarkaria made no such condition for Concurrent subjects.
Consult the states first
This is Sarkaria recommendation no. 9: consultation before Parliament legislates on a Concurrent List subject (LX p239).
State law always prevails
Under Article 254, a Central law generally prevails over a repugnant state law on a Concurrent subject; Sarkaria did not reverse this.

points: Sarkaria's approach: keep the structure, improve the working through consultation.
Punchhi later repeated the idea, asking for broad Union-state agreement before Concurrent List bills (LX p240).

POL-9.1.1-Q15.lead: Option 2 (1990): the V.P. Singh government set up the Inter-State Council under Article 263 in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's advice.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: The year the States Reorganisation Act created the Zonal Councils (statutory bodies), not the Inter-State Council.
The Janata Dal government of V.P. Singh established the Inter-State Council in 1990 (LX p253).
The year the Sarkaria Commission submitted its report recommending a permanent Inter-State Council.
The year the First ARC report recommended an Inter-State Council under Article 263; no action followed.

points: Article 263 lets the President set up an Inter-State Council; it existed on paper for 40 years before 1990.
Its chairman is the Prime Minister; members include all Chief Ministers (LX p253).

POL-9.1.1-Q16.lead: Option 4: Sarkaria wanted the All-India Services strengthened and more such services created, not abolished.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Article 356 only as a last resort
A Sarkaria recommendation: President's Rule should be used very sparingly, when all alternatives fail (LX p239).
Recommended
Residuary taxation with Parliament
A Sarkaria recommendation: residuary taxation stays with Parliament, other residuary powers go to the Concurrent List.
Recommended
A permanent Inter-State Council
A Sarkaria recommendation: a permanent Inter-Governmental Council under Article 263.
Recommended
Abolition of All-India Services
NOT Sarkaria's view; abolition was demanded by the Rajamannar Committee and the West Bengal Memorandum (LX p238).
✓ (the answer)

points: In a NOT-question, the correct option is the one that does not match the body's recommendations.
Hook: Sarkaria = strong Centre, functional reform; Rajamannar/West Bengal = abolish AIS.

POL-9.1.1-Q17.lead: Statements 1 and 2 are Sarkaria's; statement 3 is Punchhi's idea. Answer: option 3 (1 and 2 only).

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. Five-year term not disturbed
True
Sarkaria said the Governor's five-year term should not be disturbed except for extremely compelling reasons (LX p239).
2. No dismissal of a majority ministry
True
Sarkaria said the Governor cannot dismiss a Council of Ministers that commands a majority in the Assembly (LX p239).
3. Removal by impeachment by state legislature
False
This is a Punchhi Commission proposal - apply the President's impeachment procedure to Governors (LX p241); Sarkaria did not suggest it.

points: Option 1 (1 and 3) and option 2 (2 and 3) wrongly include statement 3.
Option 4 wrongly includes statement 3 as Sarkaria's.

POL-9.1.1-Q18.lead: Option 2: both Sarkaria and Punchhi wanted the Governor to be an outsider to the state and not recently active in politics.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Only Rajamannar
Rajamannar focused on state autonomy; it is not the source of the 'outsider Governor' guidelines.
Both Sarkaria and Punchhi
Sarkaria laid down that a Governor should be from outside the state and not active in politics in the recent past; Punchhi adopted these guidelines in letter and spirit (LX p241).
Only the Second ARC
The Second ARC is not known for these Governor selection guidelines.
None
Wrong: the proposal breaks two guidelines - he is from the same state and was in active politics recently.

points: Guidelines: eminent person, from outside the state, a detached figure, not too intimately connected with local politics (LX p241).
Purpose: a Governor must be neutral between the Centre and the state government.

POL-9.1.1-Q19.lead: Option 3: the Sarkaria Commission said the Zonal Councils should be constituted afresh and reactivated.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Rajamannar Committee
Tamil Nadu's 1969 committee on state autonomy; its focus was omitting Articles 356, 357, 365 and transferring subjects to states.
First ARC
The 1966 Commission (report 1969) with 22 Centre-State recommendations, headed by Inter-State Council and non-partisan Governors.
Sarkaria Commission
Recommendation no. 7: Zonal Councils to be constituted afresh and reactivated to promote federal spirit (LX p239).
Liberhan Commission
It inquired into the 1992 Babri Masjid demolition; it was not a Centre-State commission.

points: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies created by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, with five zones (LX p255).
Punchhi later asked them to meet at least twice a year (LX p242-243).

POL-9.1.1-Q20.lead: Option 3: the Second Commission on Centre-State Relations (2007) was headed by Justice Madan Mohan Punchhi, former Chief Justice of India.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Justice R.S. Sarkaria
Headed the first Centre-State commission set up in 1983.
Justice A.M. Ahmadi
A former Chief Justice of India, but he did not head the 2007 commission.
Justice M.M. Punchhi
Headed the 2007 commission, which reported in 2010 (LX p240).
Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah
Headed the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC, 2000).

points: Two Centre-State commissions: Sarkaria (1983-88) and Punchhi (2007-10).
Punchhi drew on the Sarkaria report, the NCRWC report and the Second ARC report (LX p240).

POL-9.1.1-Q21.lead: Statements 1 and 2 are true; statement 3 is false. Answer: option 2 (1 and 2 only).

head: Statement
True/False
Why
rows: 1. Report in 2010
True
The Punchhi Commission was set up in 2007 and submitted its seven-volume report in 2010 (LX p240).
2. 'Localised emergency'
True
It proposed a framework for 'localised emergency' under Article 355, so only an affected area comes under Central action and the state government continues (LX p242).
3. Governors to continue as Chancellors
False
Punchhi said the convention of Governors acting as Chancellors of universities should be done away with (LX p242).

points: Option 1 (1 and 3) and option 3 (2 and 3) wrongly include statement 3.
Option 4 includes statement 3, which is the opposite of what Punchhi said.

POL-9.1.1-Q22.lead: Option 2: the Punchhi Commission concluded that 'cooperative federalism' is the key to India's unity, integrity and development.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Competitive federalism
States compete with each other for investment and better performance; NITI Aayog promotes it through rankings (LX p672).
Cooperative federalism
Centre and states work together as partners; Punchhi called it the practical guide for Indian polity (LX p240).
A unitary system
All power with the Centre and states as mere agents; this is the opposite of federalism.
Asymmetric federalism
Some states get special provisions (for example, Article 371 states); Punchhi did not call this the key.

points: Hook: Punchhi = 'cooperative'; Granville Austin also called Indian federalism 'cooperative federalism' (LX p218).

POL-9.1.1-Q23.lead: Option 2: the Punchhi Commission said Governors should not be treated like a 'political football' removed at the Centre's will.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: A 'golden bird'
An old description of rich India; it has nothing to do with Governors.
A 'political football'
Something kicked around by parties - Governors being removed whenever the ruling party at the Centre changes.
A 'rubber stamp'
Someone who approves everything without thought; this was not Punchhi's phrase.
An 'ornamental head'
A head with only formal powers; this describes a constitutional head, not Punchhi's warning.

points: Punchhi wanted a fixed five-year tenure; removal should not be at the sweet will of the Centre (LX p241).
It suggested impeachment of Governors by a procedure like the President's (LX p241).

POL-9.1.1-Q24.lead: Answer: option 2 (both true, R does not explain A): Both true; R states the present law, A a reform proposal.

head: Part
True/False
Why
rows: A
True
Punchhi suggested impeachment-like removal of the Governor (on the lines of the President's impeachment).
R
True
Art 156: Governor holds office during the President's pleasure.

points: Does R explain A? No. R describes the problem that A wants to fix. A problem is not the explanation of a reform; it is the context.
Option 1 fails: R is true, but it does not give the reason for A.
Options 3 and 4 fail: both statements are true.

POL-9.1.1-Q25.lead: Option 2: the Chief Justice of India was not part of the committee Punchhi proposed for selecting Governors.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?

Member
Chief Justice of India
Not a member; the committee was political-executive and legislative, not judicial.
✓ (the answer)

A member, so that the state has a say in choosing its Governor.
Member
Union Home Minister
A member, as the minister in charge of Centre-State matters.
Member

Aim: to make the Governor's appointment less one-sided and more consultative.

POL-9.1.1-Q26.lead: Option 2: Punchhi said the Governor should decide within six months whether to give assent to a state bill or reserve it for the President.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1 month
No commission proposed this short limit.
6 months
Punchhi recommendation no. 12: Governor to decide within six months (LX p241).
1 year
Not a Punchhi limit; it would allow long delays.
3 months
The three-month limit came from the Supreme Court's April 2025 Tamil Nadu ruling, which the November 2025 Presidential Reference opinion set aside.

points: The six-month idea comes from Article 201, which gives the state legislature six months to reconsider a bill returned by the President; Punchhi wanted the same six months for the President too (LX p241).

POL-9.1.1-Q27.lead: Option 1: Punchhi said a pre-poll alliance should be treated as one party and, in a hung Assembly, invited first.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Treat pre-poll alliance as one party
Punchhi: a pre-poll coalition is one political party; first preference goes to the pre-poll group with the largest number (LX p241-242).
President's Rule at once
Article 356 is a last resort; a government must first be tried.
Single largest party only
The single largest party comes second, after the pre-poll alliance.
Dissolve and order fresh polls
Not the first step; the Governor must try to form a government from the elected House.

points: Order of preference: (a) pre-poll alliance with the largest number, (b) single largest party with support of others, (c) post-poll coalition with all partners in government, (d) post-poll alliance with outside support (LX p242).

POL-9.1.1-Q28.lead: All three statements are Punchhi recommendations. Answer: option 1 (1, 2 and 3).

head: Statement
True/False
Why

True

2. Zonal Councils twice a year
True

3. NIC once a year
True
Punchhi said the National Integration Council should meet at least once a year; at present its meetings have no regular schedule (LX p856).

points: Options 2, 3 and 4 each drop one true statement.
POL-9.1.1-Q28.also: It also wanted Article 263 amended to make the Inter-State Council stronger (LX p242).

POL-9.1.1-Q29.lead: Option 3: the Liberhan Commission had suggested constitutional status for the National Integration Council; the Punchhi Commission did not accept it.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Sarkaria Commission

Rajamannar Committee
Tamil Nadu's 1969 state-autonomy committee; not linked to the NIC.
Liberhan Commission
It probed the 1992 Babri Masjid demolition and suggested constitutional status for the NIC, which Punchhi rejected.
Venkatachaliah Commission
The NCRWC (2000) that reviewed the Constitution; it is not the source of this suggestion.

points: The NIC was set up in 1961 by the Central government; it is a non-constitutional body (LX p856).
Punchhi instead wanted it to meet at least once a year.

POL-9.1.1-Q30.lead: Option 1: Punchhi reformed the Governor's office (fixed tenure, impeachment procedure) but did not recommend abolishing it.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Abolition of the Governor
Not Punchhi's view; it wanted a fixed five-year tenure and removal by impeachment (LX p241).
✓ (the answer)
Equal representation in Rajya Sabha
A Punchhi recommendation: equal seats for states irrespective of population (LX p243).
Recommended
Inter-State Trade and Commerce Commission (Art 307)
A Punchhi recommendation, with binding decisions and appeal to the Supreme Court (LX p244).
Recommended
New All-India Services in health, education
A Punchhi recommendation: new AIS in health, education, engineering and judiciary (LX p243).
Recommended

points: In a NOT-question, find the option that the body never proposed.

POL-9.1.1-Q31.lead: Option 3: the Standing Committee of the Inter-State Council considered the Punchhi report in 2017 and 2018 and circulated it to the states.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: National Development Council
Set up in 1952 by executive resolution; its role passed to NITI's Governing Council and it did not examine this report (LX p675).
NITI Aayog Governing Council
A body of CMs chaired by the PM for development planning; not the body that examined Punchhi.
Standing Committee of the ISC
Took up the report in its 2017 and 2018 meetings and sent it with its views to the states (LX p244).
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs
A committee of MPs; it was not the body named for this task.

points: Logic: a Centre-State report goes to the Centre-State forum - the Inter-State Council (Art 263).

POL-9.1.1-Q35.lead: Option 2: the conclaves demanded restructuring of Centre-State relations with more powers and finances for the states.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Presidential form at the Centre
Not their demand; they wanted the federal balance changed, not the form of government.
Restructuring with greater state autonomy
The non-Congress parties, starting with NTR at Vijayawada, pressed for more powers and resources for states.
Simultaneous elections
A later debate ('One Nation, One Election'), not the theme of these conclaves.
New linguistic states

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: 1. Centre may send armed forces without State consent
A genuine Sarkaria recommendation: the Centre can deploy its forces even without State consent, though consulting the State is desirable.
2. Residuary taxation power to States
Not Sarkaria's view. It said residuary taxation stays with Parliament; only other residuary (non-tax) powers should go to the Concurrent List.
3. Governor should not dismiss a majority ministry
A genuine Sarkaria recommendation: the Governor cannot dismiss the ministry so long as it commands a majority in the Assembly.

A genuine Sarkaria recommendation: President's Rule only in extreme cases, as a last resort when all alternatives fail.

points: The question asks for the statement that does NOT reflect Sarkaria, so the one false statement is the answer.
Sarkaria (1983–88) wanted a strong Centre without over-centralisation, so it did not move taxation powers to States.
Contrast: the Rajamannar Committee (1969) and the West Bengal Memorandum (1977) wanted residuary powers given to the States.

True

False
No amendment was needed. Article 263 already lets the President set up such a council, and it was created by a Presidential order of 28 May 1990.

Option 4 (all) wrongly includes statement 3.

POL-9.1.3-Q34.lead: Option 3: Sarkaria said Article 356 is a last resort, so the State must first be warned in specific terms to correct itself.

head: Option

Wrong. The ISC is only an advisory body under Article 263; no such approval step was proposed.

Correct. The State should be warned that it is not being run according to the Constitution and given a chance to set things right.

Wrong. That is the Article 249 route for Parliament to make laws on State List subjects, not part of President's Rule.

points: Sarkaria: Article 356 should be used very sparingly, in extreme cases, only when all available alternatives fail.
Based on Sarkaria, the Supreme Court in S.R. Bommai (1994) held that imposing President's Rule without giving the State a prior warning to rectify itself (except in extreme urgency) is improper.

POL-9.1.4-Q32.lead: Option 3: Punchhi said the Governor can sanction prosecution of a State minister even against the Cabinet's advice, if the Cabinet decision appears biased.

What it is / means

Wrong. The Governor decides himself; no reference to the President is needed.

POL-9.1.4-Q33.lead: Option 3: Punchhi wanted the S.R. Bommai (1994) guidelines on Article 356 written into the Constitution.

POL-9.2.1-Q01.lead: Option 2: governments are classified as unitary or federal on the basis of relations between the national and regional governments.

head: Option
What it is / means
Correct?
rows: Method of electing head of State
Decides presidential/parliamentary or republic/monarchy, not unitary/federal.
Relationship between national and regional governments
The test: in unitary systems regions get power from the Centre; in federal systems the Constitution divides power.
